body:
## Why

The work-environment response ranks the travel policy engine as **blocked by a hosting gap**: it is described as running as an internal web service, but nothing built in that environment runs that way — every working tool is a local script, a COM-driven Office file, or a static HTML page opened locally; there is no server-hosted, database-backed application ([INFORMATION-REQUEST-RESPONSE.md §F item 17, travel policy engine](https://github.com/stranske/Ready/blob/main/research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/INFORMATION-REQUEST-RESPONSE.md)). Travel-Plan-Permission's primary surface today is `tpp-planner-service` (FastAPI + Uvicorn) at `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:2298-2359` with a hosted Render blueprint at `render.yaml:7-33`. Verified: the repo already ships a headless CLI (`fill-spreadsheet` at `README.md:35-41`) but no documented **local-first delivery shape** that avoids standing up the HTTP service. **Missing behavior:** operators in the target environment have no documented path to policy evaluation without hosting.

## Scope

Document and verify a local-first delivery alternative — local script and/or static HTML page — that delivers policy evaluation value without a hosted service, quoting the hosting constraint from the response.

## Non-Goals

Do NOT remove or deprecate `tpp-planner-service` — the hosted path remains for environments that support it.

Do NOT implement new policy rules in this issue.

Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a README paragraph without a runnable command and a smoke test is a failure.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `docs/local-first-delivery.md` quoting the hosting constraint and mapping it to this repo's surfaces.
- [ ] Document the `fill-spreadsheet` CLI path (`README.md:35-41`) as the primary local-first workflow for trip-plan JSON → Excel output without `tpp-planner-service`.
- [ ] Add `scripts/render_policy_report.py` (or extend an existing CLI) that evaluates a `TripPlan` JSON file via `PolicyEngine` and writes a static HTML report to disk without Uvicorn.
- [ ] Add `tests/python/test_local_first_delivery.py` smoke-testing the static HTML generator against `tests/fixtures/sample_trip_plan_minimal.json`.
- [ ] Update `README.md` after the Planner HTTP Service heading (`README.md:49`) with a "Local-first delivery (no hosted service)" section linking to `docs/local-first-delivery.md`.
- [ ] Test deliberate-break verification by temporarily replacing the `PolicyEngine.evaluate` call in `scripts/render_policy_report.py` with placeholder output, capture the failing test result, then revert.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/python/test_local_first_delivery.py::test_static_policy_report_is_self_contained_html` passes; generated HTML contains policy verdict text and requires no network fetch to render.
- [ ] `python scripts/render_policy_report.py tests/fixtures/sample_trip_plan_minimal.json /tmp/policy-report.html && test -s /tmp/policy-report.html` exits 0 and creates a non-empty `/tmp/policy-report.html`.
- [ ] After temporarily emitting placeholder output without calling `PolicyEngine.evaluate`, `tests/python/test_local_first_delivery.py::test_static_policy_report_is_self_contained_html` fails; the change is reverted.

## Implementation Notes

Hosting constraint source: [response §F item 17](https://github.com/stranske/Ready/blob/main/research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/INFORMATION-REQUEST-RESPONSE.md).

Local-file deep links confirmed working in [response §A Q3](https://github.com/stranske/Ready/blob/main/research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/INFORMATION-REQUEST-RESPONSE.md) — static HTML should link to local policy evidence files where applicable.

Confirmed-green local reproduction: `python -m pytest tests/python/test_http_service.py -q` passes today; the HTTP path is unchanged.

## Why

This is a latent production break: `src/travel_plan_permission/validation.py:323-325` exposes `POLICY_CONFIG`, but production evaluation calls `PolicyValidator.from_file()` at `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py:1381-1385` and no scoped production caller invokes `PolicyValidator.from_environment`. Setting the environment override therefore cannot change the planner verdict or snapshot.

## Scope

Define and implement one explicit validation-configuration override contract for production policy evaluation and versioning.

## Implementation Notes

Either consistently honor a named environment override across snapshot and final verdict paths, or remove the loader-only override. The selected source must be reflected in the policy version.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update `src/travel_plan_permission/validation.py` to expose the selected validation configuration source through one production-safe constructor.
- [ ] Update `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py` to use that constructor for snapshot and final verdict evaluation.
- [ ] Update `tests/python/test_policy_api.py` with an override-driven blocking-threshold regression case.

## Acceptance Criteria

Run pytest `tests/python/test_policy_api.py::test_check_trip_plan_honors_configured_validation_source` and confirm changing the configured budget threshold changes the verdict and snapshot status.

Temporarily bypass the configured validation source in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py` and confirm `tests/python/test_policy_api.py::test_check_trip_plan_honors_configured_validation_source` fails; revert.

## Non-Goals

Do not add mutable policy administration endpoints or change the packaged default configuration in this issue.

Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: loading an override in a standalone helper while production evaluation still uses the packaged file is a failure of this issue.
title: [P2] Wire validation configuration overrides into production evaluation

## Why

This is a latent production break: `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:418-423` treats an absent known key and a misspelled key the same, then `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:459-538` instantiates only hard-coded known rule names. A `fare_comparision` typo therefore succeeds and silently applies the default fare-comparison threshold.

## Scope

Validate policy.yaml rule names and per-rule fields before constructing the policy engine.

## Implementation Notes

Keep default values when a supported rule is omitted, but reject an unknown rule key or unknown field with a source-labeled `ValueError`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` to validate configured rule names against the supported policy rule set.
- [ ] Update `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` to validate each supported rule mapping before merging defaults.
- [ ] Update `tests/python/test_policy_engine.py` with unknown rule-name and unknown field rejection cases.

## Acceptance Criteria

Run pytest `tests/python/test_policy_engine.py::test_policy_engine_rejects_unknown_rule_configuration` and confirm `fare_comparision` raises a configuration error rather than enforcing the default threshold.

Temporarily allow the misspelled rule key through the configuration parser and confirm `tests/python/test_policy_engine.py::test_policy_engine_rejects_unknown_rule_configuration` fails; revert.

## Non-Goals

Do not rename supported policy rule identifiers or alter their configured default values.

Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: documenting supported names without rejecting unknown configuration keys is a failure of this issue.
title: [P2] Reject unknown policy rule configuration keys

## Why

This is a current break: `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:2157-2167` requires only `Permission.VIEW` and then accepts `actor_role` as the admin guard. `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:419-427` resolves that role from caller-controlled query input, while `src/travel_plan_permission/planner_auth.py:580-599` gives static tokens view/create only. The dashboard returns reviews, exceptions, audit events, and runtime posture at `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:2168-2179`.

## Scope

Authorize admin-console access from the authenticated permission set, not from a simulated role query parameter.

## Implementation Notes

Require `Permission.CONFIGURE` or a narrowly introduced admin-read permission before rendering the console. Keep `actor_role` as a display-only simulation only after that authenticated check succeeds.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` to require authenticated admin permission before rendering `/portal/admin`.
- [ ] Update `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` to ensure `actor_role` cannot determine admin-console access.
- [ ] Update `tests/python/test_http_service.py` with view-only-denied and configure-capable-allowed admin-console cases.

## Acceptance Criteria

Run pytest `tests/python/test_http_service.py::test_portal_admin_console_requires_authenticated_admin_permission` and confirm a view-only token receives 403 even with `actor_role=finance_admin`, while a configure-capable token receives 200.

Temporarily restore a view-only route requirement and confirm `tests/python/test_http_service.py::test_portal_admin_console_requires_authenticated_admin_permission` fails; revert.

## Non-Goals

Do not change the authorization rules for manager decisions or exception decisions in this issue.

Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: showing the authenticated permissions in the template while allowing a view-only token to read admin data is a failure of this issue.
title: [P1] Require authenticated admin permission for the portal admin console

## Why

This is a current break: `src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py:230-236` computes `policy_blocking_codes`, but `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:1907-1935` submits and records the proposal after checking only structural validation. `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py:1199-1240` likewise creates a pending response without calling the policy verdict.

## Scope

Prevent portal and direct policy API proposal submission when the current plan has a blocking policy verdict, while preserving evaluation of compliant and advisory-only proposals.

## Implementation Notes

Use one authoritative policy verdict at the submission boundary. Return a typed failure response or HTTP error that includes blocking codes, and do not persist a submission or manager review when that verdict fails.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` to reject portal submission when `review.policy_blocking_codes` is non-empty.
- [ ] Update `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py` to prevent `submit_proposal` from returning a pending execution for a blocking verdict.
- [ ] Update `tests/python/test_http_service.py` with a policy-blocked portal-submit regression case.
- [ ] Update `tests/python/test_policy_api.py` with a direct policy-blocked submit regression case.

## Acceptance Criteria

Run pytest `tests/python/test_http_service.py::test_portal_submit_rejects_blocking_policy_verdict` and `tests/python/test_policy_api.py::test_submit_proposal_rejects_blocking_policy_verdict`; both must show no proposal persistence for a blocking fare/evidence plan.

Temporarily remove the portal blocking-verdict guard and confirm `tests/python/test_http_service.py::test_portal_submit_rejects_blocking_policy_verdict` fails; revert.

## Non-Goals

Do not remove asynchronous evaluation for compliant proposals or redefine approval workflows.

Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: displaying blocking issues while still recording the proposal is a failure of this issue.
title: [P1] Block policy-violating portal proposals before submission

body:
## Why

`CabinClassRule.evaluate` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:233-246` compares `duration <= self.long_haul_hours`. When `duration` is `float("nan")`, both the failure branch and the long-haul exemption are false, so the rule returns `passed=True` even under blocking severity. Verified: blocking `cabin_class` with `cabin_class="premium"` and `flight_duration_hours=nan` passes. `TripPlan` rejects NaN via Pydantic (`src/travel_plan_permission/models.py:361-365`), but `PolicyContext` is unvalidated (`src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:52-80`) and `tests/baseline/adapter.py:168-177` can inject arbitrary context. This is a **latent break** on direct `PolicyContext` and baseline paths.

Prior fix: #1429 (closed 2026-08-12) covered absent inputs; a NaN `flight_duration_hours` still passes because `duration <= long_haul_hours` is False for NaN and the rule falls through to the passing branch on the current tip.

## Scope

`CabinClassRule.evaluate` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` and tests in `tests/python/test_policy_engine.py`.

## Implementation Notes

Use `math.isfinite(duration)` (or `duration is None` handling already present) before comparisons. When a flight leg is detected (`_has_flight_leg`) and duration is missing or non-finite, return `MISSING_DATA` for blocking severity (consistent with `policy.py:216-228`).

## Tasks

- [ ] Guard `CabinClassRule.evaluate` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` against non-finite `flight_duration_hours` when a flight leg is present.
- [ ] Add `test_cabin_class_blocking_rejects_nan_duration` in `tests/python/test_policy_engine.py` with blocking YAML and `PolicyContext(cabin_class="premium", flight_duration_hours=float("nan"), selected_fare=Decimal("100"))`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pytest tests/python/test_policy_engine.py::test_cabin_class_blocking_rejects_nan_duration` passes and asserts the rule does not pass with NaN duration under blocking severity.
- Temporarily remove the finite-duration guard in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` and confirm `test_cabin_class_blocking_rejects_nan_duration` fails; revert.

## Non-Goals

- Do not add Pydantic validation to `PolicyContext` in this issue.
- Do not change long-haul threshold configuration in `src/travel_plan_permission/config/policy.yaml`.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a blocking cabin rule that passes on NaN duration is a failure of this issue.
title: [P2] CabinClassRule passes when flight_duration_hours is NaN

## Why

`tests/baseline/catalog.yaml:4-6` documents only `ApprovalEngine` and `PolicyEngine` surfaces. `tests/baseline/adapter.py:190-225` runs those two engines and never `PolicyValidator.validate_plan`. Blocking `validation.yaml` rules (`ADV-001`, `BUD-001`, etc. in `src/travel_plan_permission/config/validation.yaml`) therefore have no golden or directional regression coverage. This is a **latent break** risk: validation regressions only surface in narrow unit tests.

## Scope

`tests/baseline/adapter.py`, `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml`, and new baseline test module under `tests/baseline/`.

## Implementation Notes

Add a `validation` section to the adapter flattening (e.g. `validation.n_blocking`, `validation.<code>.blocking`) or a parallel `run_validation_scenario` helper. Reuse `TripPlan` construction from `tests/python/test_validation.py::_build_plan`. Start with one enforced directional: over-budget trip fails `BUD-001`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Extend `run_scenario` or add a sibling runner in `tests/baseline/adapter.py` to call `PolicyValidator.from_file().validate_plan` on a `TripPlan` built from catalog data.
- [ ] Add a `validation_over_budget` scenario and directional entry in `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml`.
- [ ] Add `test_validation_blocking_budget` in `tests/baseline/test_validation_golden.py` asserting blocking validation metrics move in the expected direction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pytest tests/baseline/test_validation_golden.py::test_validation_blocking_budget` passes and reports a blocking validation violation for the over-budget scenario.
- Temporarily raise `trip_limit` above the scenario cost in `src/travel_plan_permission/config/validation.yaml` and confirm `test_validation_blocking_budget` fails; revert.

## Non-Goals

- Do not remove existing approval/policy baseline scenarios.
- Do not change production validation rule thresholds as the permanent fix (only for deliberate-break).
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a catalog comment claiming validation coverage without an enforced pytest gate is a failure of this issue.
title: [P2] Baseline golden/directional kit excludes validation.yaml

## Why

`diagnose_missing_inputs` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_lite.py:61-79` reports `advance_booking` missing `booking_date` when absent (`policy_lite.py:21`), but `AdvanceBookingRule.evaluate` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:150-153` returns `SKIPPED` with `passed=True` for the same context. Orchestration tests at `tests/python/test_orchestration_smoke.py:68-72` treat diagnostics as actionable missing-field blockers. This is a **latent break**: operators see missing-input errors while verdict paths treat rules as passed/skipped.

## Scope

`src/travel_plan_permission/policy_lite.py`, `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py`, tests in `tests/python/test_policy_lite.py` and `tests/python/test_orchestration_smoke.py`.

## Implementation Notes

Prefer a single source of truth: either export required-field metadata from rule classes or have `diagnose_missing_inputs` derive outcomes by calling the same missing-data branch used in `evaluate`. Align with the blocking `MISSING_DATA` fix in `policy.py` if that lands first.

## Tasks

- [ ] Align `_missing_inputs_for_rule` / `_RULE_REQUIRED_FIELDS` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_lite.py` with the outcome `PolicyEngine.validate` returns for the same context.
- [ ] Extend `test_policy_lite_reports_missing_inputs` in `tests/python/test_policy_lite.py` to assert evaluate outcome matches diagnostic severity for `advance_booking` and `local_overnight`.
- [ ] Verify `tests/python/test_orchestration_smoke.py` still passes with consistent missing-field semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pytest tests/python/test_policy_lite.py` passes with new assertions that diagnostics and `PolicyEngine.validate` agree on outcome for blocking rules with missing fields.
- Temporarily make `diagnose_missing_inputs` always emit diagnostics while `evaluate` returns `SKIPPED` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` and confirm the new `tests/python/test_policy_lite.py` assertion fails; revert.

## Non-Goals

- Do not remove `diagnose_missing_inputs` from the public API.
- Do not change validation.yaml rules.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: diagnostics that report missing fields while `evaluate` skips the rule is a failure of this issue.
title: [P2] policy_lite diagnostics disagree with PolicyEngine.evaluate for missing inputs

body:
## Why

Two classes named `AdvanceBookingRule` implement the same business concept: `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:142-164` (days between `booking_date` and `departure_date`, configured in `src/travel_plan_permission/config/policy.yaml` as 14 days advisory) and `src/travel_plan_permission/validation.py:92-138` (days between `today` and `departure_date`, configured in `src/travel_plan_permission/config/validation.yaml` as 7 days domestic blocking). `check_trip_plan` at `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py:1381-1388` runs both. A short-notice trip emits `advance_booking` (warning) and `ADV-001` (error) with different thresholds. This is a **current break** for operators expecting one advance-booking policy.

## Scope

Advance-booking evaluation path in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py`, `src/travel_plan_permission/validation.py`, `src/travel_plan_permission/config/policy.yaml`, and integration tests in `tests/python/test_policy_api.py`.

## Implementation Notes

Recommended owner: `validation.yaml` / `PolicyValidator` for submission gates. Options: (a) remove `advance_booking` from `policy.yaml` and map any planner-facing copy from validation results; (b) make `PolicyEngine` advance rule a thin wrapper that reads validation output. Preserve existing `ADV-001` code in planner issues. Update `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml` comments if policy-lite advance rule is removed.

## Tasks

- [ ] Document the single owner for advance-booking in `src/travel_plan_permission/config/policy.yaml` or remove the duplicate `advance_booking` entry from `src/travel_plan_permission/config/policy.yaml`.
- [ ] Adjust `AdvanceBookingRule` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` or remove it from `PolicyEngine.from_yaml` so `check_trip_plan` emits one advance-booking verdict.
- [ ] Update `test_check_trip_plan_enforces_validation_blocking_rules` in `tests/python/test_policy_api.py` to assert no duplicate advance-booking codes (`advance_booking` vs `ADV-001`) on the same plan.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pytest tests/python/test_policy_api.py::test_check_trip_plan_enforces_validation_blocking_rules` passes and a short-notice plan emits exactly one advance-booking issue code.
- Temporarily re-enable both advance-booking sources and confirm the duplicate-code assertion in `tests/python/test_policy_api.py` fails; revert.

## Non-Goals

- Do not change budget or duration rules in `validation.yaml`.
- Do not alter `get_policy_snapshot` validation wiring (separate issue).
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: leaving two independent advance-booking rules active in `check_trip_plan` is a failure of this issue.
title: [P2] Duplicate advance-booking rules with divergent semantics

body:
## Why

`get_policy_snapshot` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py:1130-1132` evaluates only `PolicyEngine.from_file()` and never `PolicyValidator.from_file()`. `check_trip_plan` at `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py:1381-1388` runs both engines. `portal_review.py:230-235` calls both on the same trip, so the portal can show a snapshot with `policy_status="pass"` while `check_trip_plan` fails on `BUD-001` from `validation.yaml`. Verified live: over-budget `TripPlan` includes `BUD-001` in `check_trip_plan` issues but not in `get_policy_snapshot` approval triggers. This is a **current break** on the planner snapshot / cache contract.

## Scope

`src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py` (`get_policy_snapshot`, `_policy_version`, approval trigger assembly). Tests in `tests/python/test_policy_api.py`.

## Implementation Notes

Merge `validator.validate_plan(plan)` results into `approval_triggers` using the same shape as `_issue_from_validation_result` (`src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py:576-589`). Recompute `has_blocking` and `policy_status` from both policy-lite and validation blocking results. Include validator in `_policy_version(engine, validator)` so etag reflects validation config.

## Tasks

- [ ] Load `PolicyValidator.from_file()` and call `validate_plan(plan)` inside `get_policy_snapshot` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py`.
- [ ] Append validation failures to `approval_triggers` and fold blocking validation results into `policy_status` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py`.
- [ ] Add `test_get_policy_snapshot_includes_validation_blocking_triggers` in `tests/python/test_policy_api.py` asserting `BUD-001` appears for an over-budget plan.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pytest tests/python/test_policy_api.py::test_get_policy_snapshot_includes_validation_blocking_triggers` passes for a plan with `estimated_cost` above the `validation.yaml` trip limit.
- Temporarily remove the `PolicyValidator` call from `get_policy_snapshot` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py` and confirm `test_get_policy_snapshot_includes_validation_blocking_triggers` fails; revert.

## Non-Goals

- Do not remove `validation.yaml` from `check_trip_plan` (already wired).
- Do not consolidate duplicate advance-booking rules (separate issue).
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a snapshot that omits `validation.yaml` blocking triggers while `check_trip_plan` fails is a failure of this issue.
title: [P2] get_policy_snapshot omits validation.yaml blocking controls

body:
## Why

`src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:115-116` sets `passed=True` for `RuleOutcome.SKIPPED`, and `AdvanceBookingRule.evaluate` at `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:150-153` returns `SKIPPED` when `booking_date` or `departure_date` is missing even when the rule is configured with `severity: blocking`. `LocalOvernightRule` at `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:330-333` does the same for missing `distance_from_office_miles`. `blocking_results` at `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:559-565` only counts `FAILED` and `MISSING_DATA`, so blocking rules with absent inputs never block. This is a **current break** when operators set blocking severity on these rules: verified with a blocking YAML config, `advance_booking` and `local_overnight` both return `skipped` with `passed=True`.

Prior fix: #1429 (closed 2026-08-12) added the MISSING_DATA escalation in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py`, but nine rule sites still return SKIPPED, which `_outcome` counts as passed; the residual path above is present on the current tip.

## Scope

`src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` rule outcome handling for blocking severity and missing inputs. Tests in `tests/python/test_policy_engine.py` and `tests/python/test_policy_lite.py`.

## Implementation Notes

`CabinClassRule` at `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:216-228` already returns `RuleOutcome.MISSING_DATA` for blocking severity when flight-leg fields are absent — mirror that pattern for `AdvanceBookingRule`, `LocalOvernightRule`, and `DrivingVsFlyingRule` when configured blocking. Keep `SKIPPED` for advisory severity. `check_trip_plan` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py:1386-1388` only emits issues where `not result.passed`, so fixing `passed` on missing-data outcomes is sufficient for the planner path.

## Tasks

- [ ] Change `AdvanceBookingRule.evaluate` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` to return `RuleOutcome.MISSING_DATA` with `passed=False` when `severity == Severity.BLOCKING` and required dates are absent.
- [ ] Change `LocalOvernightRule.evaluate` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` to return `RuleOutcome.MISSING_DATA` with `passed=False` when `severity == Severity.BLOCKING`, `overnight_stay` is true, and `distance_from_office_miles` is absent.
- [ ] Add `test_blocking_rules_emit_missing_data_not_skipped` in `tests/python/test_policy_engine.py` parametrizing blocking `advance_booking` and `local_overnight` with incomplete `PolicyContext`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pytest tests/python/test_policy_engine.py::test_blocking_rules_emit_missing_data_not_skipped` passes and asserts `outcome == "missing_data"` and `passed is False` for blocking rules with absent required fields.
- Temporarily restore `RuleOutcome.SKIPPED` for blocking missing-date paths in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` and confirm `test_blocking_rules_emit_missing_data_not_skipped` fails; revert.

## Non-Goals

- Do not change `validation.yaml` / `PolicyValidator` advance-booking semantics in this issue.
- Do not refactor `policy_lite.py` diagnostics (tracked separately).
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: returning `SKIPPED` with `passed=True` for blocking rules with missing inputs is a failure of this issue.

body:
## Why
This repo's aggregate line coverage is 90.26% (5,977 statements), already at or above the fleet's 90% target. **This issue is explicitly NOT about raising that percentage further.** An aggregate number can hide a completely untested critical module sitting behind many well-tested small ones — 90% overall is fully consistent with one important, complex feature being almost entirely untested. The goal is to find real risk: a feature or function whose failure would actually matter, that currently has thin or no test coverage, where a small number of well-chosen tests would meaningfully reduce the chance of a future regression going unnoticed.

## Method
1. Enumerate this repo's major features / business-critical code paths by reading its own README, entry points, and architecture docs — do not guess from the repo name or from this issue.
2. For each major feature, check ITS OWN coverage specifically (not the repo aggregate) — which files/functions implement it, and what fraction of them is actually exercised. A repo at 90.26% overall can easily have one 200-line module sitting at 20%.
3. Rank candidates by (a) how central the feature is to the app's actual purpose, (b) how complex or edge-case-prone the code is (branching logic, external I/O, state machines, data-integrity or financial calculations), and (c) how thin its real coverage is — not by raw statement count and not by how easy a test would be to write.
4. Before writing anything, confirm the top candidate is a REAL risk: read the code, articulate a concrete plausible failure (a bad input, a boundary condition, a state transition, a silent wrong answer) — not a hypothetical one. If nothing clears that bar, say so; do not manufacture a gap to fill.
5. Write ONE FOCUSED test (or a small tightly related few) pinning correct behavior for that specific risk, with the same discipline as every other round in this initiative: it must FAIL when the code is deliberately broken and PASS when reverted. Prove this for real — run the break and the revert, don't assert it.
6. If you find an ACTUAL BUG while investigating (not just a coverage gap), fix it with a minimal, targeted diff in the same PR.

## Report (required, in the PR body or a comment if no action is warranted)
Name the features you considered, which one you picked and why, the concrete failure mode the new test guards against, and what it actually proves. If no gap you found is worth closing, say so explicitly and explain why the major features are already adequately covered where it matters — that is a valid, useful outcome and is preferred over padding the number.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Named test: the new test(s), proving the identified risk is now caught.
- Deliberate-break -> revert: break the specific behavior the test targets, confirm the named test FAILS, revert, confirm it passes again. Report the transcript.

## Non-Goals
- Do NOT chase the coverage percentage — a test that pads the number without addressing a genuine breakage risk does not satisfy this issue.
- Do NOT refactor working code or touch unrelated files.
- Low blast radius only; one PR for the one risk you identify as highest-value.

_Part of the fleet coverage-calibration initiative. The goal is to improve the code, not a metric._
title: Identify undertested critical features despite 90.26% coverage (risk-based, not metric-based)

## Why
http_service.py context builders pass context keys that rendered templates never read:
- `_manager_review_queue_context` (`src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:1528-1534`) passes `role_view`, `actor_permissions`, `role_can_approve`, and `role_can_configure`, but `manager_review_queue.html` (rendered at line 1983) reads none of them.
- `_manager_review_detail_context` (`src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:1552`) passes `actor_permissions`, but `manager_review_detail.html` (rendered at lines 2017, 2059, 2087) reads 0 references.
- `_portal_admin_context` (`src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:1577`) passes `role_can_configure`, but `portal_admin.html` (rendered at line 2184) reads 0 references.
- `_portal_template_context` (`src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:1450`, dict at lines 1471-1502) passes `optional_fields`, which is read by no template in `src/travel_plan_permission/templates/` (0 hits across all template files).

Passing dead context keys creates latent fragility by implying templates enforce permissions or consume parameters when they do not. This issue resolves latent fragility rather than an active breakage.

## Non-Goals
- Template redesign or permission checking logic changes.
- Removing `ground_transport_options`, `form_action`, or `handoff_active` from `_portal_template_context`, as these keys remain live for `draft_entry.html` and `validation_feedback.html` renders.
- Scaffold-only or partial completion does not count as done for this issue: removing only some of the four dead keys, or removing keys without running `pytest tests/python/test_http_service.py` (which renders every affected template and would raise on a template referencing a removed key), is a failure of this issue.

## Tasks
- [ ] Remove `role_view`, `actor_permissions`, `role_can_approve`, and `role_can_configure` from `_manager_review_queue_context` in `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` (lines 1528-1534).
- [ ] Remove `actor_permissions` from `_manager_review_detail_context` in `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` (line 1552).
- [ ] Remove `role_can_configure` from `_portal_admin_context` in `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` (line 1577).
- [ ] Remove `optional_fields` from `_portal_template_context` in `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` (lines 1471-1502).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `pytest tests/python/test_http_service.py` exits with status code 0.
- [ ] Removing the `reviews` key from `_manager_review_queue_context` in `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` causes `pytest tests/python/test_http_service.py -k queue` to fail, and restoring `reviews` causes the test to pass.

## Implementation Notes
Validation commands:
- `pytest tests/python/test_http_service.py`
- `pytest tests/python/test_http_service.py -k queue` (for deliberate break verification)

Finish workflow:
implement -> validate -> commit -> push -> PR

## Why
The template file `src/travel_plan_permission/templates/portal_request.html` (26.7KB) is orphaned and served by no HTTP route. The live route `GET /portal/draft/new` declared at `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:1639` renders `draft_entry.html` (`src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:1643` and `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:1657`). The only references to `portal_request` across the repository are in test files: `tests/python/test_package_data.py:28`, which pins `portal_request.html` into package data distribution, and `tests/python/test_http_service.py:787` (`test_portal_request_form_get_stays_lightweight`), which is misnamed after `portal_request` but actually exercises the `/portal/draft/new` route (`draft_entry.html`). This is latent fragility and technical debt: dead weight is shipped in the wheel package data, and context key references inside `portal_request.html` create a trap misleading maintainers into believing the template is active. The pin list in `test_portal_template_resources_exist` is also stale against the live routes: it pins the dead `portal_request.html` while the live `draft_entry.html` is not pinned at all.

## Non-Goals
- No redesign or modification of `src/travel_plan_permission/templates/draft_entry.html` (adding its package-data pin is in scope; changing the template is not).
- No modifications to any other template files or HTTP route declarations.
- No addition of new HTTP routes.
- Scaffold-only or partial completion (such as deleting `src/travel_plan_permission/templates/portal_request.html` while leaving the test pin in `tests/python/test_package_data.py:28` or leaving `tests/python/test_http_service.py:787` un-renamed) does not count as done.

## Tasks
- [ ] Delete `src/travel_plan_permission/templates/portal_request.html`.
- [ ] Remove the `portal_request.html` pin at `tests/python/test_package_data.py:28` while keeping the remaining pins in `test_portal_template_resources_exist` (`portal_home.html`, `portal_expense.html`, `manager_review_queue.html`, `manager_review_detail.html`).
- [ ] Add a `draft_entry.html` pin to `test_portal_template_resources_exist` in `tests/python/test_package_data.py` (assert the file ships and contains its marker string, e.g. the draft-entry heading it renders), so the live template is guarded the way the dead one was.
- [ ] Rename `test_portal_request_form_get_stays_lightweight` at `tests/python/test_http_service.py:787` to `test_draft_entry_form_get_stays_lightweight`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `pytest tests/python/test_package_data.py` passes with `src/travel_plan_permission/templates/portal_request.html` deleted and its pin removed at `tests/python/test_package_data.py:28`.
- [ ] `pytest tests/python/test_http_service.py -k draft_entry` passes with `tests/python/test_http_service.py:787` renamed to `test_draft_entry_form_get_stays_lightweight`.
- [ ] Deliberate break test: after the `draft_entry.html` pin is added, temporarily deleting `src/travel_plan_permission/templates/draft_entry.html` causes `pytest tests/python/test_package_data.py::test_portal_template_resources_exist` to FAIL; restoring `src/travel_plan_permission/templates/draft_entry.html` returns it to passing. This proves the package-data gate still guards live templates after the removal.

## Implementation Notes
Validation commands:
1. Execute primary test gates:
   `pytest tests/python/test_package_data.py`
   `pytest tests/python/test_http_service.py -k draft_entry`
2. Perform deliberate-break verification:
   Temporarily delete `src/travel_plan_permission/templates/draft_entry.html`, run `pytest tests/python/test_package_data.py::test_portal_template_resources_exist` (confirm test failure), then restore `src/travel_plan_permission/templates/draft_entry.html` and re-run (confirm test pass).

Finish workflow:
implement -> validate -> commit -> push -> PR

body:
## Why

The policy verdict model cannot distinguish **"this rule does not apply"** from **"we lack the data to
judge"**. Every rule must return pass or fail, which forces a choice between failing open and blocking
compliant trips. Both failure modes have now occurred in this repo.

Concrete evidence:

- #1428 / #1429 fixed a family of blocking rules that **passed on absent input** (fail-open).
- #1456 then over-corrected: making `third_party_paid` fail closed on absent input reddened **10+
  golden baseline cases including `[base]`** in PR #1457, because `tests/baseline/catalog.yaml:38`
  correctly encodes `third_party_paid: (none provided) -> pass`. "No third party paid" is a
  legitimately empty collection, not missing evidence.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:173-174` currently downgrades a **blocking** `cabin_class`
  rule to `info` severity when input is absent — a workaround for the same missing concept.

There is no correct two-state answer. `SKIPPED` and `MISSING_DATA` are different facts with different
consequences: one should not block, the other must.

An independent field survey of OPA/Rego, Cerbos, JSON Logic, Oso, and Cedar
(`Code/Audits/Travel-Plan-Permission/2026-08-16-D5-policy-engines.md`) recommends exactly this
four-state model as the fix, reached independently of the #1457 regression.

## Scope

Introduce an explicit four-state rule outcome and migrate rule evaluation and verdict aggregation to it.

## Non-Goals

- Migrating to an external policy engine (OPA/Cerbos) — the same survey explicitly recommends against
  it for this codebase.
- Changing which rules are blocking, or their thresholds.
- Changing the YAML authoring format for rule configuration.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a four-state outcome (`PASSED`, `FAILED`, `SKIPPED`, `MISSING_DATA`) to the rule result model.
- [ ] Migrate each evaluator in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` to return the correct state,
      distinguishing "rule not applicable to this trip" from "required input absent".
- [ ] Define aggregation: `MISSING_DATA` on a blocking rule fails the verdict; `SKIPPED` never does.
- [ ] Remove the `cabin_class` severity-downgrade workaround (`policy.py:173-174`) once states exist.
- [ ] Scope `cabin_class` applicability to trips that actually have a flight leg (otherwise
      hotel-only and rail trips report `MISSING_DATA` rather than `SKIPPED`).
- [ ] Surface the state in the verdict payload so trip-planner can render "not applicable" distinctly
      from "needs input".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A trip with no third-party payments yields `SKIPPED` for `third_party_paid` and a passing verdict.
- [ ] A trip missing a genuinely required blocking input yields `MISSING_DATA` and a failing verdict.
- [ ] A hotel-only trip yields `SKIPPED` for `cabin_class`, not `MISSING_DATA`.
- [ ] **All existing golden baseline cases pass unchanged**, including `[base]` — the fixtures encode
      intended semantics and must not be rewritten to accommodate this change.
- [ ] No blocking rule downgrades its own severity to `info`.

## Test Gate

Named gate: `tests/python/test_policy_lite.py` — add
`test_four_state_outcomes_distinguish_skipped_from_missing_data`, parameterized over
`third_party_paid` (empty → `SKIPPED`, passing) and a blocking rule with a genuinely absent required
input (→ `MISSING_DATA`, failing).

Plus: `tests/baseline/test_golden.py` must pass with **no fixture edits**.

Deliberate-break demonstration required: collapse `SKIPPED` and `MISSING_DATA` into a single failing
state, confirm the new test **and** the golden suite fail, then revert. Paste both outputs in the PR.

## Implementation Notes

- This supersedes the `third_party_paid` half of #1456 and unblocks PR #1457, which should be
  re-scoped to `cabin_class` only (see the correction comments on both).
- The survey also recommends Hypothesis property tests over sparse inputs to catch this class
  generally; worth adding but not required to close this issue.

## Why

Two blocking rules still **pass** when their required input is absent, after the 2026-08-11 fail-open
work (#1429) fixed the rest of the family. Verified at `156ada6` during the 2026-08-16 paired audit.

- `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:173-174` — blocking `cabin_class` rule returns `passed=True`
  and downgrades severity to `info` when `cabin_class` is absent.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:343-352` — blocking `third_party_paid` rule returns
  `passed=True` when `third_party_payments` is `None`.

The sibling rules fixed by #1429 now fail closed on absent input (`policy.py:142-143`,
`policy.py:316-318`), so these two are inconsistent with the established pattern in the same file.

Impact: a trip plan that simply omits a field escapes a rule that is declared blocking.

## Scope

Make blocking `cabin_class` and `third_party_paid` fail closed on absent input, matching the
already-corrected sibling rules.

## Non-Goals

- Changing rule thresholds or which rules are blocking.
- Revisiting the `TripPlan` boundary validation fixed under #1429 (NaN/Infinity/negative), which is
  verified working.
- Broader policy-engine refactoring.

## Tasks

- [ ] Make the blocking `cabin_class` evaluator fail closed when `cabin_class` is absent
      (`policy.py:173-174`), preserving blocking severity rather than downgrading to `info`.
- [ ] Make the blocking `third_party_paid` evaluator fail closed when `third_party_payments` is
      `None` (`policy.py:343-352`).
- [ ] Confirm no non-blocking rule is changed by the same edit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A trip plan omitting `cabin_class` yields a failing verdict when the `cabin_class` rule is
      configured as blocking.
- [ ] A trip plan with `third_party_payments = None` yields a failing verdict when
      `third_party_paid` is blocking.
- [ ] Severity is not downgraded to `info` for a blocking rule on absent input.

Named gate: `tests/python/test_policy_lite.py` — add
`test_blocking_cabin_class_and_third_party_fail_closed_on_absent_input`, parameterized over both rules.

Deliberate-break demonstration required: restore the `passed=True` branch for either rule, confirm the
test **fails**, then revert. Paste both outputs in the PR.

## Implementation Notes

- The corrected pattern to copy is in the same file at `policy.py:142-143` and `policy.py:316-318`
  (the `fare_comparison` / `fare_evidence` / `non_reimbursable` fixes from #1429).

body:
## Why

The organization's travel workbook is generated **regardless of the policy verdict**. The policy check
runs, returns its result, and the document is produced anyway.

Verified in source at tip `4aa54bb`, `src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py:201-206`:

```python
policy_result = check_trip_plan(trip_plan)
artifacts = _portal_artifacts(
    canonical=canonical_plan,
    plan=trip_plan,
    answers=answers,
)
```

`policy_result` is computed on line 201 and **never consulted** before `_portal_artifacts` is called on
line 202. `grep -n "policy_result" src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py` shows it is assigned at
line 201 and passed through to the returned state at line 218 — it is never branched on.

The only condition guarding artifact creation is at
`src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py:192`:
`if not missing_fields and canonical_plan is not None and not validation_errors:` — that is **form
completeness**, not policy compliance.

The download handler does not gate either: `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:2270-2304`
authorizes the request and looks up the artifact, performing no policy-status check before serving it
with `Content-Disposition: attachment`.

Missing behavior: for a product whose purpose is enforcing an organization's travel policy before a trip
is booked, a trip the policy engine has judged non-compliant should not silently yield a completed,
downloadable employer submission document.

This is a **current break** and the same defect family as the previously-fixed budget fail-open (#1428):
the verdict is computed correctly and then not acted upon.

There is a narrow unrelated gate that should not be mistaken for this one: submission refuses a plan
whose own `TripStatus` is `REJECTED` at `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py:830-855`. That is a
submission gate, not a workbook or download gate, and it does not make a `check_trip_plan()` failure
block the artifact path.

## Scope

`src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py` — where the verdict is computed and the artifacts built.

`src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` — the artifact download routes.

`tests/python/test_portal_review.py` — where the gating assertions belong.

## Non-Goals

Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding a status check that only affects a log line, a label,
or the returned state while `_portal_artifacts` still runs and the download still serves, is a failure
of this issue. The deliberate-break criterion below must be demonstrated.

Do not block the workbook on advisory-severity findings; only a blocking verdict should gate.

Do not remove the existing `TripStatus.REJECTED` submission gate; it is separate and correct.

Do not change the download route's authorization model.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update the `portal_review.py` module docstring to document whether a blocking policy verdict prevents artifact generation, prevents download, or both.
  - [ ] Document in the portal_review.py module docstring that blocking policy verdicts prevent artifact generation (verify: docs updated)
  - [ ] Document in the portal_review.py module docstring the behavior when advisory-severity findings are present (verify: docs updated)
- [ ] Gate `_portal_artifacts` in `src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py` on the blocking status of `policy_result`.
- [ ] Update the state returned from `src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py` to name the blocking issue codes when no document is produced.
- [ ] Add a compliance check to the artifact download handler in `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` so a previously-generated artifact cannot be fetched after a verdict turns blocking.
- [ ] Add `test_workbook_is_not_generated_for_a_blocking_verdict` to `tests/python/test_portal_review.py`.
- [ ] Add `test_workbook_download_refuses_a_blocking_verdict` to `tests/python/test_portal_review.py`.
- [ ] Add `test_advisory_findings_do_not_block_the_workbook` to `tests/python/test_portal_review.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_portal_review.py::test_workbook_is_not_generated_for_a_blocking_verdict -q` passes.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_portal_review.py::test_workbook_download_refuses_a_blocking_verdict -q` passes.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_portal_review.py::test_advisory_findings_do_not_block_the_workbook -q` passes.
- [ ] A trip that `check_trip_plan()` reports as blocking produces no downloadable artifact, and the returned state names the blocking codes.
- [ ] Remove the new gate in `src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py`, run `python -m pytest tests/python/test_portal_review.py::test_workbook_is_not_generated_for_a_blocking_verdict -q`, and confirm it fails; restore the gate and confirm it passes.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/ -q` reports no new failures versus the baseline count recorded in the PR.

## Implementation Notes

`check_trip_plan()` already returns a `PolicyCheckResult` whose `status` is `"fail"` when any rule of
blocking severity failed, so the gate needs no new evaluation — only a branch on the value already in
hand at `src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py:201`.

Consider whether a blocked trip should still produce a *draft marked non-compliant* rather than
nothing; that is a product decision worth recording in the docstring either way.

````text
- `src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py` — where the verdict is computed and the artifacts built.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` — the artifact download routes.
- `tests/python/test_portal_review.py` — where the gating assertions belong.

## Non-Goals

- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding a status check that only affects a log line, a label,
  or the returned state while `_portal_artifacts` still runs and the download still serves, is a failure
  of this issue. The deliberate-break criterion below must be demonstrated.
- Do not block the workbook on advisory-severity findings; only a blocking verdict should gate.
- Do not remove the existing `TripStatus.REJECTED` submission gate; it is separate and correct.
- Do not change the download route's authorization model.

## Tasks

- [ ] Decide and document, in the `portal_review.py` module docstring, whether a blocking policy verdict prevents artifact generation, prevents download, or both.
- [ ] Gate `_portal_artifacts` at `src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py:202` on the blocking status of `policy_result`.
- [ ] Return a state from `src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py` that names the blocking issue codes, so a caller can explain why no document was produced.
- [ ] Add a compliance check to the artifact download handler at `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:2270` so a previously-generated artifact cannot be fetched after a verdict turns blocking.
- [ ] Add `test_workbook_is_not_generated_for_a_blocking_verdict` to `tests/python/test_portal_review.py`.
- [ ] Add `test_workbook_download_refuses_a_blocking_verdict` to `tests/python/test_portal_review.py`.
- [ ] Add `test_advisory_findings_do_not_block_the_workbook` to `tests/python/test_portal_review.py` so the gate is not over-broad.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_portal_review.py::test_workbook_is_not_generated_for_a_blocking_verdict -q` passes.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_portal_review.py::test_workbook_download_refuses_a_blocking_verdict -q` passes.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_portal_review.py::test_advisory_findings_do_not_block_the_workbook -q` passes.
- [ ] A trip that `check_trip_plan()` reports as blocking produces no downloadable artifact, and the returned state names the blocking codes, captured in the PR.
- [ ] Deliberate-break demonstration: remove the new gate at `src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py:202`, run `python -m pytest tests/python/test_portal_review.py::test_workbook_is_not_generated_for_a_blocking_verdict -q` and confirm it FAILS, then restore and confirm it passes. Paste both runs in the PR.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/ -q` reports no new failures versus the baseline count recorded in the PR.

## Implementation Notes

- `check_trip_plan()` already returns a `PolicyCheckResult` whose `status` is `"fail"` when any rule of
  blocking severity failed, so the gate needs no new evaluation — only a branch on the value already in
  hand at `src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py:201`.
- Consider whether a blocked trip should still produce a *draft marked non-compliant* rather than
  nothing; that is a product decision worth recording in the docstring either way.
````
</details>

title: The organization workbook is generated regardless of the policy verdict

body:
## Why

The durable audit record and the state change it describes are not atomic, so **the audit trail can
assert that a trip was approved when the approval never persisted.** In a travel-approval system the
audit trail is the evidence of who approved what, so a record that survives a failed action is a
false attestation.

This is a **current break, reproduced** at tip `426f041`. Forcing the portal-state persistence call to
fail during an approval, then reloading state from the store:

```
caught                = forced portal-state persistence failure
in_memory_status      = approved
reloaded_status       = pending_manager_review
durable_action_events = 1
```

The durable audit event recording the approval was written and survived. The approval itself did not.
A reader of the audit trail therefore sees an approval for a trip whose persisted state is still
`pending_manager_review`.

The same investigation found the reverse failure is also reachable: a **successful** export can have
its audit event lost, so the trail can under-report real actions as well as over-report unreal ones.

**One adjacent claim was checked and REFUTED, and should not be re-raised.** It was suspected that an
audit event is appended *before* input validation, which would produce a false trail on every rejected
request. That is not the case. An invalid request returns HTTP 400 and writes only a truthful
`auth.request` record:

```
http_status              = 400
new_durable_event_types  = [('auth.request', 'success')]
durable_action_events     = 0
in_memory_review_events   = 0
```

So ordering relative to validation is correct. The defect is specifically **atomicity between the
audit write and the state write**, not ordering.

Missing behavior: an audit event describing an action must be durable if and only if the action is
durable. Neither direction currently holds.

## Scope

- `src/travel_plan_permission/audit.py` — durable audit event writing.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` — the approval and review handlers that mutate state
  and append audit events.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py` — the review state transitions.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sql_store.py` — the snapshot persistence the audit write is
  not joined to.
- `tests/python/test_audit.py` — where the atomicity assertions belong.

This is **distinct from the already-filed concurrency issue**, which covers multi-writer transaction
collisions and lost updates. This issue is single-threaded atomicity between two writes, and it
reproduces with one writer.

## Non-Goals

- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: wrapping the two writes in a `try` block that logs and
  continues, leaving an approval audit event durable after the state write failed, is a failure of this
  issue. Both deliberate-break criteria below must be demonstrated.
- Do not re-report or re-fix the concurrent lost-update behavior; that has its own issue.
- Do not change the ordering relative to validation; it is already correct, as shown above.
- Do not drop audit events to achieve atomicity; the goal is that both land or neither does.
- Do not weaken the audit trail's durability guarantees for the success path.

## Tasks

- [ ] Decide and document the atomicity contract between a state mutation and its audit record in the `src/travel_plan_permission/audit.py` module docstring.
- [ ] Join the audit append and the state persistence into one transactional unit in `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` for the approval path, so a persistence failure discards the audit event.
- [ ] Apply the same transactional joining to the review-transition path in `src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py`.
- [ ] Ensure a successful action cannot lose its audit event in `src/travel_plan_permission/audit.py`, by writing the event inside the same committed unit as the state change.
- [ ] Add `test_audit_event_is_discarded_when_state_persistence_fails` to `tests/python/test_audit.py`, forcing the persistence call to raise and asserting no durable action event remains.
- [ ] Add `test_audit_event_survives_a_successful_action` to `tests/python/test_audit.py` asserting the success path records exactly one durable action event.
- [ ] Add `test_invalid_request_writes_no_action_audit_event` to `tests/python/test_audit.py` to lock in the currently-correct ordering behavior so it cannot regress.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_audit.py::test_audit_event_is_discarded_when_state_persistence_fails -q` passes, and `durable_action_events` is 0 after a forced failure, replacing the observed value of 1.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_audit.py::test_audit_event_survives_a_successful_action -q` passes.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_audit.py::test_invalid_request_writes_no_action_audit_event -q` passes.
- [ ] After a forced persistence failure, the reloaded state and the durable audit trail agree: no approval is recorded for a trip whose state remains `pending_manager_review`, captured in the PR.
- [ ] Deliberate-break demonstration: separate the audit append from the state persistence again in `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py`, run `python -m pytest tests/python/test_audit.py::test_audit_event_is_discarded_when_state_persistence_fails -q` and confirm it FAILS, then restore and confirm it passes. Paste both runs in the PR.
- [ ] Deliberate-break demonstration: suppress the audit write on the success path, run `python -m pytest tests/python/test_audit.py::test_audit_event_survives_a_successful_action -q` and confirm it FAILS, then restore and confirm it passes.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/ -q` reports no new failures versus the baseline count recorded in the PR.

## Implementation Notes

- Runnable probes for both the confirmed atomicity break and the refuted ordering claim are preserved
  outside this repository in the audit record at
  Code/Audits/Travel-Plan-Permission/2026-08-11-assets/ as `probe-audit-atomicity.py` and
  `probe-invalid-request.py`. The atomicity probe monkeypatches the persistence call to raise, which is
  a test-time patch rather than a source change.
- Sequencing: the open concurrency issue changes how the store commits, and this issue changes what is
  committed alongside the audit event. Doing that one first is likely to make this one simpler, since a
  single lock-guarded write path is an easier place to join the two writes.

title: Audit record and state change are not atomic: the trail can assert an approval that never persisted

body:
## Why

Two modules combine request parsing, domain transitions, rendering, persistence orchestration and
route wiring in a single file each, and both are growing rather than shrinking. Every open defect in
this repository currently lands in one of them, so the cost is paid repeatedly.

Measured at tip `426f041`, against the 2026-07-10 baseline:

| File | 2026-07-10 | now | direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` | 2,538 | 2,546 | grew |
| `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py` | 1,857 | 1,898 | grew |

The 2026-07-10 audit measured route-registration functions at cyclomatic complexity 12 to 17,
`_expense_review_state` at 16, `_populate_travel_workbook` at 20, and auth-configuration parsing at
25. `_populate_travel_workbook` is still defined at
`src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py:1686`.

Missing behavior: there is no size or complexity guard, so each fix adds to the same two files. The
41 lines `policy_api.py` gained today came from a correct fix, which is the point: the modules absorb
every change because nothing pushes back.

This is **latent fragility, not a current break** — the test suite passes and behavior is correct.
Recorded as TPP-04 on 2026-07-10 and still open.

## Scope

- `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` — route wiring, portal state, request handling.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py` — policy evaluation, mapping, workbook population.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py` — an existing extraction target boundary.
- `tests/python/test_http_service.py` — characterization coverage for the HTTP surface.
- `tests/python/test_policy_api.py` — characterization coverage for the policy surface.

## Non-Goals

- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: creating new modules that merely re-export from
  `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py`, or moving code while the two file sizes stay above
  the recorded threshold, is a failure of this issue. The measured acceptance gate below must be met.
- Do not change any route contract, request schema, or response shape; this is a structural change
  only.
- Do not attempt both modules in one commit; extract behind characterization tests incrementally.
- Do not renumber or reword existing issue codes while moving the rules that emit them.
- Do not begin this work while the open policy correctness and concurrency issues are unmerged; they
  touch these same files and rebasing a large extraction over them wastes effort.

## Tasks

- [ ] Record the current line counts and the highest-complexity functions for `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` and `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py` in the PR as the baseline.
- [ ] Add characterization tests to `tests/python/test_http_service.py` asserting the current response shape of each registered route before any code moves.
- [ ] Add characterization tests to `tests/python/test_policy_api.py` covering `check_trip_plan` and the workbook population path before any code moves.
- [ ] Extract the workbook population logic starting at `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py:1686` into a dedicated module under `src/travel_plan_permission/`, leaving the public name importable.
- [ ] Extract the expense-review state machine out of `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` into a dedicated module, leaving route behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Extract the auth-configuration parsing out of `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` into a dedicated module.
- [ ] Split route registration in `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` so each route group registers from its own module.
- [ ] Add a measured size and complexity guard to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that fails when a changed function in `src/travel_plan_permission/` exceeds a recorded threshold.
- [ ] Add `test_module_sizes_stay_under_threshold` to `tests/python/test_policy_api.py` asserting the recorded line-count ceiling for both modules.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_http_service.py -q` passes with the characterization assertions intact.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_policy_api.py -q` passes with the characterization assertions intact.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_policy_api.py::test_module_sizes_stay_under_threshold -q` passes, with both files measurably smaller than the baseline recorded in the PR.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/ -q` reports the same pass count as the pre-change baseline recorded in the PR, with no route contract change.
- [ ] Deliberate-break demonstration: add a function to `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` that pushes it back over the recorded threshold, run `python -m pytest tests/python/test_policy_api.py::test_module_sizes_stay_under_threshold -q` and confirm it FAILS, then remove it and confirm it passes. Paste both runs in the PR.
- [ ] The complexity guard added to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` fails on a deliberately over-complex function and passes once it is reverted, with both runs captured in the PR.

## Implementation Notes

- The measured guard is the part that matters. The sibling repository filed the same decomposition
  twice, closed both COMPLETED on the same day, and its route component still grew by 343 lines
  afterwards, because nothing enforced the direction. Land the guard early, even if the extraction is
  incremental.
- Sequencing: the open policy correctness, fail-open and concurrency issues all modify these two
  files. Doing this last avoids rebasing a large structural change over them.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py` already exists as a separate module and is a useful
  precedent for where a boundary can sit.

body:
## Why

A built wheel omits two runtime configuration files the package cannot start without, so the planner
verdict entry point raises `FileNotFoundError` in any installed deployment.

This is a **current break, verified by building and installing an actual wheel** at tip `426f041`:

```
policy.yaml            ABSENT from wheel
validation.yaml        ABSENT from wheel
approval_rules.yaml    PRESENT inside the wheel's packaged config directory
excel_mappings.yaml    PRESENT inside the wheel's packaged config directory
```

Installed into a fresh virtual environment, from outside any source checkout:

```
PolicyEngine.from_file()       FileNotFoundError: No policy.yaml configuration file found
PolicyValidator.from_file()    FileNotFoundError: No validation.yaml file found
check_trip_plan()              FileNotFoundError: No policy.yaml configuration file found
```

Verified cause: `pyproject.toml:79` declares package data including `config/*.yaml`, but only
`approval_rules.yaml` and `excel_mappings.yaml` exist under
`src/travel_plan_permission/config/`. `policy.yaml` and `validation.yaml` live only in the
repository-root `config/` directory, which is outside the package, and the engines locate them by
searching parent directories of the source tree rather than through packaged resources.

**This became more severe today.** PR #1430 wired `validation.yaml` into the planner verdict path, so
`check_trip_plan` at `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py:1679` now calls
`PolicyValidator.from_file()` in addition to `PolicyEngine.from_file()`. The verdict path therefore
now depends on two unpackaged files instead of one.

Missing behavior: the default engines must construct from an installed distribution without a source
checkout. `ApprovalEngine` already demonstrates the packaged-resource pattern in this codebase.

Recorded as TPP-02 on 2026-07-10 and still open. Latent for the current deployment, which runs from a
source checkout, but a hard break for any wheel, sdist, or slim container.

## Scope

- `pyproject.toml` — the package-data declaration.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` — `PolicyEngine` default-path resolution.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/validation.py` — `PolicyValidator` default-path resolution.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/config/` — the packaged config directory the files must move into.
- `config/policy.yaml` and `config/validation.yaml` — the current repository-root locations.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py` — the verdict path that now needs both files.

## Non-Goals

- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding a glob to `pyproject.toml` while
  `policy.yaml` and `validation.yaml` still live only outside the package, or a change that passes
  in an editable install but not from a built wheel, is a failure of this issue. The wheel-install
  acceptance gate below must be demonstrated.
- Do not remove the explicit path-override behavior; callers that pass a path must keep working.
- Do not duplicate the files in two locations that can drift; pick one home and reference it.
- Do not address the fail-open rule behavior here; that is a separate open issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Move or copy `config/policy.yaml` to `src/travel_plan_permission/config/policy.yaml` so it sits inside the package.
- [ ] Move or copy `config/validation.yaml` to `src/travel_plan_permission/config/validation.yaml` so it sits inside the package.
- [ ] Change the default-path resolution in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` to load the packaged resource via `importlib.resources`, keeping the parent-directory search only as a development fallback.
- [ ] Change the default-path resolution in `src/travel_plan_permission/validation.py` to load the packaged resource via `importlib.resources`, keeping the parent-directory search only as a development fallback.
- [ ] Confirm the explicit-path override still takes precedence in both `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` and `src/travel_plan_permission/validation.py`.
- [ ] Decide whether the repository-root `config/policy.yaml` remains as the editable source of truth or is removed, and record the decision in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py`.
- [ ] Add `test_default_engines_construct_from_installed_wheel` to `tests/python/test_policy_api.py` that constructs both engines with the source-tree parent search disabled.
- [ ] Add a wheel-contents assertion to `tests/python/test_policy_api.py` covering `policy.yaml` and `validation.yaml`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_policy_api.py::test_default_engines_construct_from_installed_wheel -q` passes.
- [ ] Building a wheel, installing it into a separate virtual environment, and running `python -c "from travel_plan_permission.policy_api import check_trip_plan; print('ok')"` from an unrelated working directory exits zero, with the transcript captured in the PR.
- [ ] From that same wheel install, constructing `PolicyEngine.from_file()` and `PolicyValidator.from_file()` both succeed, captured in the PR, replacing the two `FileNotFoundError` results recorded above.
- [ ] Inspecting the built wheel shows both YAML files present under the packaged config directory, captured in the PR.
- [ ] Deliberate-break demonstration: remove `policy.yaml` from the packaged config directory, run `python -m pytest tests/python/test_policy_api.py::test_default_engines_construct_from_installed_wheel -q` and confirm it FAILS, then restore and confirm it passes. Paste both runs in the PR.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/ -q` reports no new failures versus the baseline count recorded in the PR.

## Implementation Notes

- The captured wheel-install transcript is stored outside this repository in the audit record at
  Code/Audits/Travel-Plan-Permission/2026-08-11-assets/proof-wheel-missing-config.txt.
- Note that a `chdir` away from the checkout is NOT a valid reproduction: the parent-directory search
  walks up from the module file, not the working directory, so an editable install still finds the
  files. Only a real wheel install in a separate environment reproduces this.
- `ApprovalEngine` in this package already implements the packaged-resource fallback; mirror it.
- The matching trip-planner issue 1675 was the same defect class in the sibling repository and has
  already been fixed there; its PR is a useful reference.

body:
## Why

The organization's real travel itinerary form is committed to this repository and is not used. The
active template is still the generated placeholder.

This is a **current break, verified** at tip `6ea4a5e5`:

- `src/travel_plan_permission/config/excel_mappings.yaml:5` sets
  `template_file: travel_request_template.xlsx` under template id `ITIN-2025.1`.
- `templates/travel_request_template.xlsx` is the 5,293-byte generated placeholder, whose rendered
  output is an unformatted grid of clipped `<<field_name>>` tokens with no human-readable labels.
- `templates/Travel_Itinerary_Form_Jan_1_2026_revised.xlsx` — the organization's actual form — is
  present in the repository.
- `templates/Expense_Report_Form_FY2026_revised_Jan_2026.xlsx` — the post-trip reimbursement form —
  is also present.
- `grep -rn "Travel_Itinerary_Form" src/` returns nothing, so the real form has no consumer
  anywhere in the package.

Missing behavior: the workbook a user generates and hands to their workplace must be built from the
organizational form, and today is built from the placeholder while the genuine form sits inert
beside it. Recorded as TPP-05 on 2026-07-10; the fix was completed on the unmerged branch
`codex/organizational-workbook-canary`, so `main` never received it.

## Scope

- `src/travel_plan_permission/config/excel_mappings.yaml` — the active template pointer.
- `templates/travel_request_template.xlsx` — the placeholder currently in use.
- `templates/Travel_Itinerary_Form_Jan_1_2026_revised.xlsx` — the organizational source form.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/mapping.py` — field mapping to workbook cells.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py` — `_populate_travel_workbook` and the schema it fills.
- `tests/python/test_spreadsheet_fill.py` — existing workbook coverage.

The completed implementation exists on branch `codex/organizational-workbook-canary` at commit
`02fc4f7b`, currently 1 commit ahead of `main` and 24 behind, 37 files changed and 1,382
insertions. It adds an OOXML renderer that changes only declared input and formula cells while
copying every other workbook ZIP member unchanged, a no-submission canary, the versioned intake
catalog, the review-only handoff, and a layout-preserving runtime derivative recorded with source
and runtime SHA-256 values. Prefer rebasing and merging that work over rebuilding it.

## Non-Goals

- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: repointing `src/travel_plan_permission/config/excel_mappings.yaml`
  at the organizational form without a passing guard test, or producing a workbook that still
  contains an unresolved `<<field_name>>` token, is a failure of this issue. The deliberate-break
  criterion below must be demonstrated.
- Do not rebuild the OOXML renderer from scratch; it exists on the branch and was verified in Excel.
- Do not substitute `templates/Expense_Report_Form_FY2026_revised_Jan_2026.xlsx` for the pre-trip
  itinerary request; they are distinct artifacts.
- Do not let `openpyxl.save()` or a LibreOffice resave rewrite the template; both destroyed the
  layout, which is why the OOXML approach exists.
- Do not modify `templates/Travel_Itinerary_Form_Jan_1_2026_revised.xlsx`; it must stay
  byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Do not add a submission step; the canary must stop before submission.

## Tasks

- [ ] Rebase branch `codex/organizational-workbook-canary` onto current `main`, resolving the 24 commits of drift including the synced workflow templates under `.github/workflows/`.
- [ ] Update `template_file` in `src/travel_plan_permission/config/excel_mappings.yaml:5` to the organizational runtime derivative rather than `travel_request_template.xlsx`.
- [ ] Record `source_sha256` and `runtime_sha256` provenance keys in `src/travel_plan_permission/config/excel_mappings.yaml` so a generated placeholder cannot silently replace the real form again.
- [ ] Decide the fate of `templates/travel_request_template.xlsx`: delete it, or mark it in `src/travel_plan_permission/config/excel_mappings.yaml` as a fixture that cannot be the active template.
- [ ] Add `test_active_template_is_not_the_placeholder` to `tests/python/test_spreadsheet_fill.py` asserting the configured `template_file` is not `travel_request_template.xlsx`.
- [ ] Add `test_generated_workbook_has_no_unresolved_placeholder_tokens` to `tests/python/test_spreadsheet_fill.py` asserting no `<<` token survives in a generated workbook.
- [ ] Add `test_source_template_sha256_matches_config` to `tests/python/test_spreadsheet_fill.py` asserting the recorded `source_sha256` matches the committed `templates/Travel_Itinerary_Form_Jan_1_2026_revised.xlsx`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_spreadsheet_fill.py::test_active_template_is_not_the_placeholder -q` passes.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_spreadsheet_fill.py::test_generated_workbook_has_no_unresolved_placeholder_tokens -q` passes.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_spreadsheet_fill.py::test_source_template_sha256_matches_config -q` passes.
- [ ] Deliberate-break demonstration: set `template_file` back to `travel_request_template.xlsx` in `src/travel_plan_permission/config/excel_mappings.yaml:5`, run `python -m pytest tests/python/test_spreadsheet_fill.py::test_active_template_is_not_the_placeholder -q` and confirm it FAILS, then revert and confirm it passes. Paste both runs in the PR.
- [ ] Live-verification gate: generate one workbook, open it in Microsoft Excel, confirm formulas recalculate and no mapped region is clipped, and capture the observed city/state and total-trip-estimate values in the PR body.
- [ ] `git diff --stat` on `templates/Travel_Itinerary_Form_Jan_1_2026_revised.xlsx` after a generation run shows no change, captured in the PR.
