body:
## Why

The planner service shares one portal-state store, and therefore one `sqlite3.Connection`, across
all its synchronous FastAPI routes. Concurrent writes on that shared connection collide, and the
snapshot-write design destroys other writers' records even when they do not collide.

This is a **current break, reproduced** at tip `6ea4a5e5`. Twelve concurrent `save_snapshot` calls
released simultaneously from a `threading.Barrier`:

```
A. Production topology: one shared store
   succeeded=1  failed=11
     x9  OperationalError: cannot start a transaction within a transaction
     x1  OperationalError: not an error
     x1  OperationalError: cannot commit - no transaction is active

B. Test topology: a new store per thread
   succeeded=12  failed=0

C. Lost update via full-snapshot replace
   after writer A: ['draft-A']   after writer B: ['draft-B']   draft-A LOST
```

Experiment B matters: `tests/python/test_portal_state_store.py:177` builds
`SQLitePortalStateStore` inside each worker, so every thread gets its own connection and the
test passes 12/12. Production shares one, so CI cannot see this.

Two independent verified causes:

1. `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sqlite_store.py:188` issues a bare `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`
   on the shared connection with no lock. The connection is built at
   `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sqlite_store.py:67` with `check_same_thread=False`
   and `isolation_level=None`, disabling Python's own guardrail. The trailing
   `not an error` and `cannot commit` results show a failed writer can leave the shared
   connection's transaction state corrupted for subsequent writers.
2. `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sql_store.py:34` calls `_delete_absent_records` for
   each namespace, making every write a whole-namespace replace. Serializing the transaction does
   not fix this; experiment C needed no concurrency at all.

The single store is created at `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:2479` and closed over
by every route. This was recorded as TPP-01 on 2026-07-10 with the identical measurement (1 of 12),
so it is stable across a month and 20+ commits.

## Scope

- `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sqlite_store.py` — connection construction and the
  `_transaction` context manager.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sql_store.py` — `save_snapshot` whole-namespace replace.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/postgres_store.py` — same one-connection-per-store shape.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` — the shared store in `create_app`.
- `tests/python/test_portal_state_store.py` — the test whose topology hides this.

## Non-Goals

- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: serializing the transaction so the 12 writers stop
  raising `OperationalError` while writer B still deletes writer A's record is a failure of this
  issue. Both named acceptance tests must pass.
- Do not fix this by only changing the existing test to share one store.
- Do not convert the service to async purely to serialize writes.
- Do not disable WAL journal mode.
- Do not swallow `OperationalError` with a bare retry that leaves the lost update in place.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a write lock or request-scoped connection strategy to `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sqlite_store.py` so two threads cannot both enter `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on one connection.
- [ ] Document the chosen concurrency model in the `SQLitePortalStateStore` class docstring in `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sqlite_store.py`.
- [ ] Ensure a failed write cannot leave a partial transaction open, by resetting connection state in the `_transaction.__exit__` error path at `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sqlite_store.py:192`.
- [ ] Replace the whole-namespace delete in `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sql_store.py:34` with per-record deltas or a snapshot-version check so a writer cannot delete records it never saw.
- [ ] Apply the same lock or connection strategy to `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/postgres_store.py`, or record in its class docstring why it is unaffected.
- [ ] Rewrite `test_reconcile_is_transactional_for_threaded_writers` in `tests/python/test_portal_state_store.py:177` to share ONE store across all worker threads.
- [ ] Add `test_shared_singleton_store_survives_concurrent_writes` to `tests/python/test_portal_state_store.py` asserting 12 concurrent writers through one shared store all succeed.
- [ ] Add `test_concurrent_writers_do_not_lose_each_others_records` to `tests/python/test_portal_state_store.py` asserting two writers adding distinct records from the same base snapshot both survive.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_portal_state_store.py::test_shared_singleton_store_survives_concurrent_writes -q` passes with 12 of 12 writers succeeding and zero `OperationalError`.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_portal_state_store.py::test_concurrent_writers_do_not_lose_each_others_records -q` passes.
- [ ] Deliberate-break demonstration: remove the write lock added to `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sqlite_store.py`, run `python -m pytest tests/python/test_portal_state_store.py::test_shared_singleton_store_survives_concurrent_writes -q` and confirm it FAILS with `cannot start a transaction within a transaction`, then restore and confirm it passes. Paste both runs in the PR.
- [ ] Deliberate-break demonstration: restore the whole-namespace delete at `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sql_store.py:34`, run `python -m pytest tests/python/test_portal_state_store.py::test_concurrent_writers_do_not_lose_each_others_records -q` and confirm it FAILS, then restore and confirm it passes.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/ -q` reports no new failures versus the baseline count recorded in the PR.

## Implementation Notes

- A runnable three-experiment reproduction is stored outside this repository in the audit record
  at Code/Audits/Travel-Plan-Permission/2026-08-11-assets/proof-concurrency-shared-store.py. It
  prints a verdict line and doubles as the before/after check for the criteria above.
- SQLite with a single writer connection is a reasonable design at this service's scale; the
  cheapest correct fix may be an explicit single-writer, lock-guarded, per-record-delta store
  rather than a connection pool.

body:
## Why

Blocking travel-policy rules pass when their inputs are absent or non-finite. Because `TripPlan` arrives from an untrusted HTTP boundary, a client can defeat a blocking rule by omitting a field or sending `NaN`.

This is a current break, verified at tip `6ea4a5e5`: `fare_comparison` passes without `lowest_fare`; `cabin_class` passes without or with `NaN` `flight_duration_hours`, although matched controls fail.

Verified causes: `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:141`, `:172`, and `:176` fail open; `src/travel_plan_permission/models.py:351` permits non-finite numeric values. `tests/python/test_policy_api.py:266` currently protects the defect.

## Scope

`src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` (`fare_comparison`, `cabin_class`, `non_reimbursable`); `src/travel_plan_permission/models.py` (`TripPlan` numeric constraints); `config/policy.yaml` blocking severities; `tests/python/test_policy_api.py`; `tests/python/test_policy_lite.py`.

## Non-Goals

Do not treat finite-number validation alone as completion if absent `lowest_fare` or `NaN` duration still reports `status="pass"`. Do not fail-close advisory rules, reject all optional `None` fields, or address unwired `config/validation.yaml` rules.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add finite, non-negative constraints to `flight_duration_hours`, `distance_from_office_miles`, `driving_cost`, `flight_cost`, `selected_fare`, and `lowest_fare` in `src/travel_plan_permission/models.py`.
- [ ] Update `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` to return HTTP 422 for non-finite or negative numeric values.
- [ ] Update `fare_comparison` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:141` to fail closed with a distinct issue code when `lowest_fare` is absent.
- [ ] Update `cabin_class` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:172` to fail closed with a distinct issue code when `flight_duration_hours` is absent.
- [ ] Update `non_reimbursable` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:312` to fail closed when `expenses` is omitted.
- [ ] Update `test_check_trip_plan_skips_cost_comparison_when_estimates_missing` in `tests/python/test_policy_api.py:266` to assert fail-closed behavior.
- [ ] Add `test_blocking_rules_fail_closed_on_absent_or_nonfinite_input` to `tests/python/test_policy_lite.py` covering absent `lowest_fare`, absent `flight_duration_hours`, `NaN`, both infinities, and a negative value.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `python -m pytest tests/python/test_policy_lite.py::test_blocking_rules_fail_closed_on_absent_or_nonfinite_input -q` passes.
- [ ] `TripPlan(flight_duration_hours=float("nan"))` raises a Pydantic validation error rather than constructing.
- [ ] A business-cabin request without `flight_duration_hours` does not return `status="pass"` from `check_trip_plan`.
- [ ] Reverting `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:172` to pass when `flight_duration_hours is None` makes `test_blocking_rules_fail_closed_on_absent_or_nonfinite_input` fail; restoring it makes the test pass.
- [ ] `python -m pytest tests/python/ -q` reports no new failures versus the recorded baseline, accounting for the repointed test.

## Implementation Notes

A runnable six-case reproduction is in `Code/Audits/Travel-Plan-Permission/2026-08-11-assets/proof-failopen-absent-and-nan-inputs.py`.

`allow_inf_nan=False` may be the smallest change; confirm route validation returns HTTP 422 rather than 500. Bare comparison guards do not catch `NaN`; use `math.isfinite` with explicit range checks.

<details>
<summary>Original Issue</summary>

```text
## Why

Blocking travel-policy rules pass when their inputs are absent or non-finite. Because `TripPlan`
arrives from an untrusted HTTP boundary, a client can defeat a blocking rule by omitting a field
or sending `NaN`.

This is a **current break, verified by runtime execution** at tip `6ea4a5e5`. Each case below was
run with a matched control proving the rule fires when data is present:

| Input | Verdict | Control | Control verdict |
|-------|---------|---------|-----------------|
| `selected_fare=900`, `lowest_fare=None` | **pass** | `lowest_fare=200` | `fail (fare_comparison)` |
| `cabin_class="business"`, `flight_duration_hours=None` | **pass** | `flight_duration_hours=2.0` | `fail (cabin_class)` |
| `cabin_class="business"`, `flight_duration_hours=NaN` | **pass** | `flight_duration_hours=-50.0` | `fail (cabin_class)` |

Both rules are `severity: blocking` in `config/policy.yaml`. Verified causes:

- `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:141` returns a passing result for `fare_comparison` when
  fare data is missing.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:172` returns a passing result for `cabin_class` when
  flight details are missing.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:176` compares `duration <= long_haul_hours`, which is
  `False` for `NaN`, so the restriction branch is skipped.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/models.py:351` declares these numeric fields as plain
  `float | None` / `Decimal | None` with no finiteness or non-negativity constraint, and Pydantic
  accepts `NaN` without complaint.

The NaN case proves this is a finiteness gap rather than an intentional skip-on-missing policy: a
negative duration is correctly caught while `NaN` is not.

Missing behavior: a blocking rule whose required input is absent or non-finite must not report
compliance. Note `tests/python/test_policy_api.py:266` currently asserts the skip behavior, so CI
protects the defect.

## Scope

- `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` — `fare_comparison`, `cabin_class`, `non_reimbursable`.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/models.py` — `TripPlan` numeric field constraints.
- `config/policy.yaml` — the severities that make these rules blocking.
- `tests/python/test_policy_api.py` — the test that encodes the current fail-open.
- `tests/python/test_policy_lite.py` — rule-level coverage.

## Non-Goals

- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding finite-number types without making an
  absent-`lowest_fare` or `NaN`-duration plan stop reporting `status="pass"` is a failure of this
  issue. The deliberate-break criterion below must be demonstrated.
- Do not flip advisory-severity rules to fail-closed in this issue.
- Do not add a blanket reject-all-`None` guard that breaks legitimately optional fields.
- Do not address the unwired `config/validation.yaml` rules here; that is a separate issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add finite and non-negative constraints to `flight_duration_hours` in `src/travel_plan_permission/models.py:351` so `NaN`, both infinities, and negative values are rejected at the model boundary.
- [ ] Add the same finite and non-negative constraints to `distance_from_office_miles`, `driving_cost`, `flight_cost`, `selected_fare` and `lowest_fare` in `src/travel_plan_permission/models.py`.
- [ ] Return HTTP 422 for a non-finite or negative numeric value in `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` rather than evaluating a policy verdict.
- [ ] Change `fare_comparison` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:141` to fail closed when `lowest_fare` is absent, emitting a distinct issue code.
- [ ] Change `cabin_class` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:172` to fail closed when `flight_duration_hours` is absent, emitting a distinct issue code.
- [ ] Change `non_reimbursable` in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:312` to fail closed when `expenses` is omitted.
- [ ] Repoint `test_check_trip_plan_skips_cost_comparison_when_estimates_missing` in `tests/python/test_policy_api.py:266` to assert the new fail-closed behavior.
- [ ] Add `test_blocking_rules_fail_closed_on_absent_or_nonfinite_input` to `tests/python/test_policy_lite.py` covering absent `lowest_fare`, absent `flight_duration_hours`, `NaN`, both infinities, and a negative value.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_policy_lite.py::test_blocking_rules_fail_closed_on_absent_or_nonfinite_input -q` passes.
- [ ] A `TripPlan` with `flight_duration_hours=float("nan")` raises a Pydantic validation error instead of constructing, verified by `python -c` in the PR body showing the raised error.
- [ ] A business-cabin request with no `flight_duration_hours` does not return `status="pass"` from `check_trip_plan`, shown by the named test above.
- [ ] Deliberate-break demonstration: revert `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py:172` to return a passing result when `flight_duration_hours` is `None`, run `python -m pytest tests/python/test_policy_lite.py::test_blocking_rules_fail_closed_on_absent_or_nonfinite_input -q` and confirm it FAILS, then restore and confirm it passes. Paste both runs in the PR.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/ -q` reports no new failures versus the baseline count recorded in the PR, with the one repointed test accounted for explicitly.

## Implementation Notes

- A runnable reproduction covering all six cases with their controls is stored outside this
  repository in the audit record at
  Code/Audits/Travel-Plan-Permission/2026-08-11-assets/proof-failopen-absent-and-nan-inputs.py.
- `allow_inf_nan=False` on the field or model is the smallest change, but confirm it surfaces as
  HTTP 422 rather than a 500 at the route.
- Bare `< 0` / `> 1` guards are insufficient because every comparison against `NaN` is `False`;
  prefer `math.isfinite` plus an explicit range.
```

body:
## Why

The organization's travel budget cap is configured and never enforced on the path the planner
calls. `config/validation.yaml` defines `BUD-001` with `trip_limit: 5000` and `blocking: true`,
but the planner-facing verdict path cannot evaluate it.

This is a **current break, verified by runtime execution** at tip `6ea4a5e5` — not latent
fragility. A plan that satisfies every blocking rule in `config/policy.yaml` (fare evidence
attached, two hotel comparisons, economy cabin, booked 61 days ahead) but costs $99,999 against
the $5,000 blocking limit produces:

```
check_trip_plan()  ->  status = "pass",  issues = []
PolicyValidator    ->  ("BUD-001", "error", blocking=True,
                        "Estimated cost 99999 exceeds trip limit 5000")
```

Three verified causes:

1. `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py:1648` constructs only `PolicyEngine.from_file()`;
   `PolicyValidator` is never constructed on this path.
2. `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py:829` builds `PolicyContext` without
   `estimated_cost`, and `PolicyContext` declares no total-cost field, so the planner-facing
   engine is structurally incapable of evaluating a spend cap.
3. `src/travel_plan_permission/models.py:407` `run_validation()` is the only route to
   `PolicyValidator` and has zero production callers.

Missing behavior: a trip exceeding the configured blocking budget must return
`status="fail"` with `BUD-001`, and today returns `status="pass"` with an empty issue list.
`config/policy.yaml` contains no budget rule and no duration rule at all.

## Scope

- `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py` — `check_trip_plan` and `_context_from_plan`.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` — `PolicyContext` field set.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/models.py` — `run_validation`.
- `config/validation.yaml` — `BUD-001`, `DUR-001`, `ADV-001`, `PROV-001`.
- `config/policy.yaml` — the rule set actually evaluated today.
- Affected consumers: `src/travel_plan_permission/portal_review.py`,
  `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py` `get_evaluation_result`.

## Non-Goals

- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a change that constructs `PolicyValidator` on the
  verdict path but does not make a $99,999 trip return `status="fail"` with `BUD-001` is a
  failure of this issue. The deliberate-break criterion below must be demonstrated.
- Do not merge `config/policy.yaml` and `config/validation.yaml` into one file here.
- Do not change the HTTP response shape beyond adding the missing issues.
- Do not rewrite `PolicyEngine` or `PolicyValidator`; wire them.
- Do not address the absent-input and NaN fail-open behavior here; that is a separate issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a `estimated_cost` field to the `PolicyContext` dataclass in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy.py` so total trip cost is available to rule evaluation.
- [ ] Populate `estimated_cost` from `plan.estimated_cost` in `_context_from_plan` at `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py:829`.
- [ ] In `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py`, make `check_trip_plan` also evaluate `config/validation.yaml` blocking rules and merge them into `PolicyCheckResult.issues`.
- [ ] In `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py`, set `PolicyCheckResult.status` to `"fail"` when any merged `config/validation.yaml` result has `blocking=True`.
- [ ] In `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py`, include merged blocking results in `blocking_issues` on `PlannerProposalEvaluationResult`.
- [ ] Document the intended division of labour between `PolicyEngine` and `PolicyValidator` in the `check_trip_plan` docstring in `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py`.
- [ ] Add `test_check_trip_plan_enforces_validation_blocking_rules` to `tests/python/test_policy_api.py` asserting a $99,999 trip against `trip_limit: 5000` returns `status="fail"` including code `BUD-001`.
- [ ] Add `test_every_blocking_validation_rule_is_reachable` to `tests/python/test_policy_api.py` asserting each `blocking: true` rule in `config/validation.yaml` can be triggered through `check_trip_plan`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_policy_api.py::test_check_trip_plan_enforces_validation_blocking_rules -q` passes, and the same trip previously returned `status="pass"`.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/test_policy_api.py::test_every_blocking_validation_rule_is_reachable -q` passes.
- [ ] Deliberate-break demonstration: raise `trip_limit` in `config/validation.yaml` from `5000` to `200000`, run `python -m pytest tests/python/test_policy_api.py::test_check_trip_plan_enforces_validation_blocking_rules -q` and confirm it FAILS on the `BUD-001` assertion, then revert the value and confirm it passes. Paste both runs in the PR.
- [ ] Running `python -m pytest tests/python/ -q` reports no new failures versus the pre-change baseline count recorded in the PR.
- [ ] `PolicyContext` exposes a total-cost field, verified by `python -c "from travel_plan_permission.policy import PolicyContext; print('estimated_cost' in PolicyContext.__dataclass_fields__)"` printing `True`.

## Implementation Notes

- A runnable reproduction is stored outside this repository in the audit record at
  Code/Audits/Travel-Plan-Permission/2026-08-11-assets/proof-BUD001-fails-open.py and prints
  the pass/fail verdict plus the `BUD-001` result for the same plan.
- `run_validation` in `src/travel_plan_permission/models.py` mutates `self.validation_results`
  as a side effect; if you call it from the verdict path, decide deliberately whether that
  mutation is wanted.
- `config/policy.yaml` already carries an `advance_booking` rule that overlaps `ADV-001`, so
  advance booking is covered today; budget and duration are the genuine gaps.

body:
## Why

`docs/GOALS.md` still lists "Gate job pattern: ❌ Blocked" in its "What Works Now" table (line 113), a stale entry from the repo's 2025-12-22 setup phase. The section heading immediately above it (line 27) was already amended to read "RESOLVED," but the table row was never updated. The same file's open Tasks list (lines 136–141) includes "Re-enable actionlint, docs-lint, schema-validate jobs" — jobs that have run on every PR for months via `pr-00-gate.yml`. `docs/ci-system-guide.md`'s Local Jobs table (lines 84–90) enumerates only six jobs (actionlint, docs-lint, link-check, schema-validate, python-ci, gate) and its architecture diagram (lines 26–38) shows three local jobs; both omit the `orchestration` job ("LangGraph Orchestration CI," `ci.yml:35`) and `cross-repo-smoke` job (`ci.yml:63`) that run on every push and PR. `docs/agent-integration-status.md` declares "Full Belt automation: ❌ Not available … Would require workflow duplication" (line 15), yet `.github/workflows/` now contains `agents-71-codex-belt-dispatcher.yml`, `agents-72-codex-belt-worker.yml`, `agents-73-codex-belt-conveyor.yml`, `agents-80-pr-event-hub.yml`, `agents-81-gate-followups.yml`, and `agents-issue-intake.yml`. This is **latent fragility, not a current break**: CI and belt automation work correctly today, but an agent reading these three docs would attempt to add the LangGraph job that already exists, or conclude the gate is broken.

## Scope

- Update `docs/GOALS.md`'s "What Works Now" table (lines 104–113) to mark "Gate job pattern" ✅ Works, add rows for the LangGraph Orchestration CI job (`ci.yml:35`) and Cross-Repo Smoke job (`ci.yml:63`), and check off the open Tasks items (lines 136–141) that are already done.
- Update `docs/ci-system-guide.md`'s Local Jobs table (lines 84–90) and architecture diagram (lines 26–38) to include the `orchestration` (LangGraph Orchestration CI) and `cross-repo-smoke` jobs present in `ci.yml`.
- Update `docs/agent-integration-status.md`'s Integration Matrix (lines 7–15) to reflect that full belt automation is active via the thin-caller workflows now present in `.github/workflows/`.
- Leave `docs/CI_SYSTEM_GUIDE.md` (the synced Workflows template) untouched — it is managed from `stranske/Workflows`.

## Non-Goals

- Do not edit `ci.yml`, `pr-00-gate.yml`, or any workflow YAML — this is a documentation-only fix.
- Do not consolidate `docs/ci-system-guide.md` and `docs/CI_SYSTEM_GUIDE.md`; both currently exist with different content serving different audiences.
- Do not update workflow-sync or template-sync docs — those belong in `stranske/Workflows`.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: updating only one or two of the three stale docs while leaving the others unchanged is a partial completion and fails this issue. All three files must be updated and the deliberate-break criterion below must be demonstrated.

body:
## Why

`docs/contracts/planner-integration.md:219-235` (§5, "Persist planner-runtime follow-up state") requires that when `trip-planner` submits a proposal through the orchestration smoke path, the policy result must be persisted in `travel_plan_permission.orchestration.graph.TripState` with `planner_turn`, `policy_result`, `checkpoint_metadata`, and `follow_up_action` populated. The `run_cross_repo_smoke` function at `src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py:370` already calls `client.fetch_evaluation_result()` and receives a `PlannerProposalEvaluationResult`, but never constructs or persists a `TripState` from that result. The `_assert_state_store_reloads` helper at `cross_repo_smoke.py:255-282` only checks `proposals_by_execution_id`, `proposal_id`, and `trip_id` in the portal state store; there is no TripState shape in `RECORD_NAMESPACES` (`persistence/store.py:11-18`), and `http_service.py` imports nothing from `orchestration.graph`. This is **latent fragility, not a current break**: `test_policy_graph_persists_planner_runtime_seam` (`tests/python/test_orchestration_smoke.py:75`) proves TripState serialization works for the local `run_policy_graph` path, but no test covers the HTTP evaluation → TripState → portal store → reload chain that the contract requires.

## Scope

- Extend `run_cross_repo_smoke` in `src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py` to construct a `TripState` from the evaluation result immediately after the `fetch_evaluation_result` call at line 370, and persist it through the existing `resolve_portal_state_store` boundary.
- Add or extend `_assert_state_store_reloads` at `cross_repo_smoke.py:255` (or add a companion `_assert_trip_state_reloads`) to reload a fresh store snapshot and assert the four required TripState fields survive.
- Extend `test_cross_repo_smoke_proves_submission_status_evaluation_and_reload` at `tests/python/test_cross_repo_smoke.py:170` to assert the reloaded TripState shape alongside the existing proposal/evaluation reload checks.
- Confirm the CI job at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:182` (`tpp-cross-repo-smoke`) exercises the new assertion without weakening the existing reload checks.

## Non-Goals

- Do not redesign the public planner proposal/status/evaluation API (`src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py`) or replace `StoredProposal` in `proposals_by_execution_id`.
- Do not require `trip-planner` to write TripState; this is scoped to TPP-side persistence keyed by `execution_id`.
- Do not refactor `http_service.py` to invoke `run_policy_graph` internally unless a separate design change calls for that.
- Do not add a new `trip_states_by_execution_id` entry to `RECORD_NAMESPACES` in `persistence/store.py` unless persistence analysis confirms it is needed; a keyed JSON sidecar alongside the existing snapshot is acceptable.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a green `tpp-cross-repo-smoke` run that never asserts TripState fields from `store.load_snapshot()` is a failure of this issue. The deliberate-break acceptance criterion below must be demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py`, add an import of `TripState` from `travel_plan_permission.orchestration.graph` and, after `client.fetch_evaluation_result()` at line 370, construct a `TripState` with `planner_turn={"source": "trip_planner", "execution_id": execution_id}`, `policy_result` derived from `evaluation.outcome` and `evaluation.blocking_issues`, `checkpoint_metadata={"state_model": "TripState", "trip_id": trip_id, "policy_status": evaluation.outcome}`, and `follow_up_action={"source": "policy_check", "execution_id": execution_id, "trip_id": trip_id, "policy_status": evaluation.outcome, "required": True}`.
- [ ] In `src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py`, persist the constructed `TripState` (via `state.model_dump_json()`) through `resolve_portal_state_store(resolved_state_path)` — write it keyed by `execution_id` into the store snapshot — then call `store.close()`.
- [ ] Add `_assert_trip_state_reloads` in `src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py` that accepts `state_path`, `execution_id`, `trip_id`, and `expected_outcome`, reloads a fresh store via `resolve_portal_state_store`, and asserts `planner_turn["source"] == "trip_planner"`, non-empty `policy_result`, `checkpoint_metadata["state_model"] == "TripState"`, and a populated `follow_up_action["execution_id"]`.
- [ ] Call `_assert_trip_state_reloads` inside `run_cross_repo_smoke` in `cross_repo_smoke.py` immediately after the existing `_assert_state_store_reloads` call at line 357, passing `resolved_state_path`, `execution_id`, `trip_id`, and `evaluation.outcome`.
- [ ] In `tests/python/test_cross_repo_smoke.py:170-198` (`test_cross_repo_smoke_proves_submission_status_evaluation_and_reload`), add assertions after line 198 that reload `store.load_snapshot()` and confirm the TripState shape: `planner_turn["source"] == "trip_planner"`, `checkpoint_metadata["state_model"] == "TripState"`, and `follow_up_action["policy_status"] == result.outcome`.
- [ ] Add a focused test `test_cross_repo_smoke_persists_trip_state_after_evaluation` in `tests/python/test_cross_repo_smoke.py` that runs `run_cross_repo_smoke` with `_LivePlannerTransport`, then asserts TripState fields from a fresh `resolve_portal_state_store(state_path).load_snapshot()` call, mirroring the pattern in `test_policy_graph_persists_planner_runtime_seam` at `test_orchestration_smoke.py:75-122`.
- [ ] In `docs/contracts/planner-integration.md` under §5 (line ~235), add one sentence citing `src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py` and the `tpp-cross-repo-smoke` CI job as the integration-level evidence that this persistence contract is satisfied.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest tests/python/test_cross_repo_smoke.py::test_cross_repo_smoke_proves_submission_status_evaluation_and_reload -q` passes, with the new assertions on `checkpoint_metadata["state_model"] == "TripState"` and `planner_turn["source"] == "trip_planner"` exercised.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** temporarily stub out the TripState construction block added in `cross_repo_smoke.py` (e.g. comment out the `TripState(...)` call and its `store.save_snapshot` write). With this change, `tests/python/test_cross_repo_smoke.py::test_cross_repo_smoke_proves_submission_status_evaluation_and_reload` **must FAIL** with a `KeyError` or `AssertionError` on the TripState lookup. Revert the break; both the extended existing test and the new `test_cross_repo_smoke_persists_trip_state_after_evaluation` pass. Capture the FAIL output in the PR.
- [ ] `pytest tests/python/test_cross_repo_smoke.py tests/python/test_orchestration_smoke.py -q` passes with all existing proposal/evaluation reload assertions intact — no regressions in `test_policy_graph_persists_planner_runtime_seam`.
- [ ] `rg "TripState" src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py` returns at least one import line and one construction site, confirming the orchestration model is wired into the smoke (not tested only in isolation).
- [ ] The CI step at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:182` (`Run tpp-cross-repo-smoke`) exits 0 with the new TripState assertion active.

## Implementation Notes

- `src/travel_plan_permission/orchestration/graph.py:26-41` — `TripState` Pydantic model; all target fields (`planner_turn`, `policy_result`, `checkpoint_metadata`, `planner_feedback`, `follow_up_action`) are `dict[str, object] | None` and serializable via `model_dump_json()`.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py:48-57` — `CrossRepoSmokeResult` dataclass; may need an optional `trip_state_persisted: bool` field to surface TripState persistence in the result summary.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py:255-282` — `_assert_state_store_reloads`; add `_assert_trip_state_reloads` as a parallel helper with the same signature pattern.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py:357-383` — the full post-submit assertion+evaluation block; TripState construction and persistence go after line 372.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/__init__.py` — exports `resolve_portal_state_store`; already imported in `cross_repo_smoke.py:14`.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/store.py:11-18` — `RECORD_NAMESPACES`; check whether a new namespace is needed for TripState storage or whether the existing snapshot dict can carry it as a keyed entry.
- `tests/python/test_cross_repo_smoke.py:170-198` — existing test to extend; add TripState reload assertions after line 198.
- `tests/python/test_orchestration_smoke.py:75-122` — reference for TripState assertion shape: `checkpoint_metadata["state_model"] == "TripState"`, `follow_up_action["source"] == "policy_check"`, `model_dump_json()` + `model_validate_json()` round-trip.
- `docs/contracts/planner-integration.md:219-235` — §5 contract commitment; add cross-reference once gap is closed.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:182-192` — `Run tpp-cross-repo-smoke` and `Run tpp-planner-smoke` steps; no workflow changes expected unless a separate orchestration-persistence job is warranted.

- Extend `test_cross_repo_smoke_proves_submission_status_evaluation_and_reload` at `tests/python/test_cross_repo_smoke.py:170` to assert the reloaded TripState shape alongside the existing proposal/evaluation reload checks.

## Non-Goals

- Do not require `trip-planner` to write TripState; this is scoped to TPP-side persistence keyed by `execution_id`.
- Do not refactor `http_service.py` to invoke `run_policy_graph` internally unless a separate design change calls for that.
- Do not add a new `trip_states_by_execution_id` entry to `RECORD_NAMESPACES` in `persistence/store.py` unless persistence analysis confirms it is needed; a keyed JSON sidecar alongside the existing snapshot is acceptable.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a green `tpp-cross-repo-smoke` run that never asserts TripState fields from `store.load_snapshot()` is a failure of this issue. The deliberate-break acceptance criterion below must be demonstrated.

- `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/__init__.py` — exports `resolve_portal_state_store`; already imported in `cross_repo_smoke.py:14`.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/store.py:11-18` — `RECORD_NAMESPACES`; check whether a new namespace is needed for TripState storage or whether the existing snapshot dict can carry it as a keyed entry.

# Move the 5-second wall-clock export assertion out of the unit-test lane

## Why
`Travel-Plan-Permission/tests/python/test_export_service.py` contains
`test_exports_complete_within_five_seconds_for_typical_batch`, a hard wall-clock assertion that an export
batch finishes within 5 seconds. Wall-clock assertions in the unit lane flake on slow/loaded
environments: this test **failed** during a full local run on a cloud-synced filesystem (export pulls in
reportlab/openpyxl, whose import + I/O cost varies widely by host). Missing/wrong behavior: a
machine-speed-dependent assertion gates the unit suite, so a green codebase reports red purely due to host
speed. **Latent fragility, not a logic break** — the export output is correct; only the timing assertion
is environment-sensitive.

## Scope
Relocate the timing assertion out of the default unit run into a dedicated, opt-in performance lane (a
`perf` pytest marker excluded by default, or a separate perf test module not collected by the standard
run). The functional export assertions in the same test stay in the unit lane.

## Non-Goals
- Do NOT delete the performance check — keep it runnable on demand (it has value as a perf guard).
- Do NOT change export behavior or output format.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: leaving the 5s assertion in the default-collected unit run (or
  deleting it outright) is a failure. The gate below must show it is no longer in the default run yet still
  runnable.

## Tasks
- [ ] In `Travel-Plan-Permission/tests/python/test_export_service.py`, mark
  `test_exports_complete_within_five_seconds_for_typical_batch` with a `perf` marker (register `perf` in
  `pyproject.toml`/`pytest.ini`) and configure the default run to deselect `perf` (e.g. `addopts = -m "not perf"`).
- [ ] Keep/duplicate the functional (non-timing) assertions for that batch in the unit lane so coverage of
  the export *result* is unaffected.
- [ ] Document the opt-in command (`pytest -m perf`) in the test module docstring or the test README.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The timing test is excluded from the default run: `pytest tests/python/test_export_service.py -q`
  collects and runs the functional cases but **not**
  `test_exports_complete_within_five_seconds_for_typical_batch` (confirm via `--collect-only` that the perf
  test is deselected by default).
- [ ] The perf test is still runnable: `pytest -m perf tests/python/test_export_service.py` collects and
  runs exactly the timing test (non-zero collected count).
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** temporarily remove the `-m "not perf"` default deselection; the default
  `pytest tests/python/test_export_service.py --collect-only` then **includes** the perf test (proving the
  deselection is what removes it). Revert. Capture both collect-only outputs.

## Implementation Notes
- Verify the exact test name/path against current `Travel-Plan-Permission` `main` before editing.
- This is the TPP half of the former combined audit finding #13 (the trip-planner score-clamp half is a
  separate trip-planner issue).

body:
# Remove the type:ignore cluster in TPP orchestration graph.py

## Why

`src/travel_plan_permission/orchestration/graph.py` carries **13 of TPP's 18
`# type: ignore` comments in `src/`** (verified on `main`:
`git show origin/main:src/travel_plan_permission/orchestration/graph.py | grep
-cE 'type:\s*ignore'` = 13; whole-`src` total = 18, with the remaining 5 split
`demo_seed.py`=4, `validation.py`=1). Twelve of the thirteen are
`# type: ignore[return-value]` on a `return value` line inside a
`_coerce_*`/`_serialize_*` method whose body has narrowed everything except the
final fallthrough, e.g. `_coerce_plan` (`graph.py:45` signature
`-> dict[str, object]`, ignore at `graph.py:50`), and the matching
`_serialize_plan` (`graph.py:127`, ignore at `graph.py:150` region). The
thirteenth is `state.unfilled_mapping_report = report  # type:
ignore[assignment]` (`graph.py:259`).

The repo is type-checked under `[tool.mypy]` with `strict = true`
(`pyproject.toml:144`) and **`warn_unused_ignores = true`**
(`pyproject.toml:146`), `python_version = "3.12"` (`pyproject.toml:143`), and
mypy is the documented type-check gate for CI (`ci.yml:7` header; run via the
`Python CI` job that delegates to
`stranske/Workflows/.github/workflows/reusable-10-ci-python.yml@main` at
`ci.yml:28`).

Missing/wrong behavior: each `return value  # type: ignore[return-value]`
returns a value still statically typed `object` from a method annotated to
return a concrete shape (`dict[str, object]`, `str | None`, etc.); the ignore
suppresses the real mismatch instead of the body proving the type (via
`isinstance` narrowing, `cast`, or a typed fallback). Because
`warn_unused_ignores = true`, these ignores are also load-bearing in the wrong
direction — they cannot simply be deleted; the underlying type must be made
provable first, then the ignore removed in the same change.

This is **latent fragility, not a current break**: mypy passes today (the
ignores suppress the diagnostics), and runtime behavior is unaffected. The
defect is that 13 real return/assignment type mismatches are hidden behind
blanket ignores in the single most ignore-dense module in `src/`, so a genuine
return-type regression in any `_coerce_*`/`_serialize_*` method would be
silently swallowed by the same ignore.

## Scope

Make the return/assignment types in `graph.py` statically provable and remove
all 13 `# type: ignore` comments from the file, so the module type-checks under
the existing strict mypy config with zero ignores. Apply narrowing (`isinstance`
guards / explicit `cast` from `typing` / typed local variables) inside the
`_coerce_*` (`graph.py:45`–`graph.py:124` region) and `_serialize_*`
(`graph.py:127`–`graph.py:162` region) methods and at the
`unfilled_mapping_report` assignment (`graph.py:259`) so each annotated return /
assignment type is satisfied without suppression. `graph.py`-only; no behavior,
signature, or public-API changes elsewhere.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change the runtime behavior of any `_coerce_*`/`_serialize_*` method or
  the values they return — narrowing/casting only, same outputs for the same
  inputs.
- Do NOT change the annotated return types in the method signatures
  (e.g. `_coerce_plan -> dict[str, object]`); satisfy them, do not relax them.
- Do NOT touch the 5 remaining `src/` ignores in `demo_seed.py` (4) or
  `validation.py` (1), nor any ignore outside `src/`
  (`scripts/`, `tools/`, `tests/`) — those are separate surfaces and out of
  scope here.
- Do NOT weaken the mypy config to make ignores unnecessary — `strict = true`
  (`pyproject.toml:144`) and `warn_unused_ignores = true` (`pyproject.toml:146`)
  must stay exactly as-is.
- Scaffold-only / partial completion does NOT count for THIS issue: removing
  some but not all 13 ignores, deleting an ignore while leaving the underlying
  mismatch (so mypy errors), or swapping `[return-value]` for a broader blanket
  `# type: ignore` is a failure. The file must reach **0** `type: ignore`
  occurrences AND mypy must pass, and the deliberate-break gate below must be
  demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `graph.py:45` `_coerce_plan` (annotated `-> dict[str, object]`),
  replace the `return value  # type: ignore[return-value]` at `graph.py:50`
  with a narrowed/cast return that proves `dict[str, object]` (e.g. an
  `isinstance(value, dict)` guard plus `cast`), removing the ignore.
- [ ] Apply the same narrowing-then-remove to the remaining `[return-value]`
  ignores in the `_coerce_*` methods: `_coerce_canonical_plan` (`graph.py:54`),
  `_coerce_spreadsheet_path` (`graph.py:65`), `_coerce_policy_result`
  (`graph.py:74`), `_coerce_policy_missing_inputs` (`graph.py:85`),
  `_coerce_runtime_record` (`graph.py:106`), `_coerce_unfilled_mapping_report`
  (`graph.py:115`).
- [ ] Apply the same to the `_serialize_*` methods: `_serialize_plan`
  (`graph.py:127`), `_serialize_canonical_plan` (`graph.py:133`),
  `_serialize_spreadsheet_path` (`graph.py:139`),
  `_serialize_policy_missing_inputs` (`graph.py:145`),
  `_serialize_unfilled_mapping_report` (`graph.py:157`) — removing each
  `[return-value]` ignore.
- [ ] Fix the assignment at `graph.py:259`
  (`state.unfilled_mapping_report = report  # type: ignore[assignment]`) by
  giving `report` a type that matches the `TripState.unfilled_mapping_report`
  field annotation (`graph.py:26` `class TripState(BaseModel)`), removing the
  `[assignment]` ignore.
- [ ] Perform the deliberate-break verification (see Acceptance Criteria),
  capture the FAIL output, then revert the break before requesting review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Zero-ignore gate (observable, grep-based):
  `git show HEAD:src/travel_plan_permission/orchestration/graph.py | grep -cE
  'type:\s*ignore'` returns **0** (down from 13).
- [ ] Named command passes: `python -m mypy
  src/travel_plan_permission/orchestration/graph.py` reports **0 errors** under
  the existing `[tool.mypy]` config (`strict = true`,
  `warn_unused_ignores = true`); equivalently the `Python CI` mypy gate
  (`ci.yml:28`, `reusable-10-ci-python.yml@main`) is green on the PR.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** in any one fixed method (e.g.
  `_coerce_spreadsheet_path`, `graph.py:65`, annotated `-> str | None`),
  temporarily introduce a real type error — change the proven return to
  `return 0` (an `int`, violating `str | None`). With that change and the ignore
  already removed, `python -m mypy
  src/travel_plan_permission/orchestration/graph.py` **must FAIL** with a
  `[return-value]` error on that line. Revert the break; mypy returns to 0
  errors. Capture both runs.
- [ ] Behavior-unchanged regression gate: the orchestration test suite stays
  green — `pytest tests/orchestration_graph_test.py -q` reports 0 failed (same
  pass count as before the change).

## Implementation Notes

- The 12 `[return-value]` sites share one shape: a method narrows with
  `isinstance`/`model_dump(...)` on the happy paths, then has a final
  `return value` where `value: object` is still wider than the declared return.
  The fix is to make the fallthrough provable (guard + `cast`, or restructure so
  the last branch returns an already-narrowed local), not to add a different
  ignore.
- `warn_unused_ignores = true` (`pyproject.toml:146`) means you cannot delete an
  ignore in isolation: if you remove an ignore but the mismatch persists you get
  a `[return-value]`/`[assignment]` error, and if you fix the mismatch but leave
  the ignore you get an `unused "type: ignore"` error. Both must move together
  per site.
- Confirmed against current `main`: 13 `type: ignore` in `graph.py`
  (lines 50, 61, 70, 81, 96, 111, 124, 130, 136, 142, 154, 162 `[return-value]`
  + 259 `[assignment]`); `src/` total = 18; `[tool.mypy]` at `pyproject.toml:142`
  with `strict`/`warn_unused_ignores` true; `mypy>=2.1.0`
  (`pyproject.toml:38`).
- Confirmed-green local reproduction (from repo root, dev extras installed):
  `python -m mypy src/travel_plan_permission/orchestration/graph.py` passes today
  (because the ignores suppress the errors); `pytest
  tests/orchestration_graph_test.py -q` passes today.
title: Remove the type:ignore cluster in TPP orchestration graph.py

# Split the 799-line create_app god-function in http_service.py

## Why

`create_app` in `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:1672` is a single
function that spans lines 1672–2492 (verified on `main`: the next top-level
`def main` begins at `http_service.py:2493`) — **784 non-blank lines** (`git show
origin/main:src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py | awk 'NR>=1672 &&
NR<=2492 && NF>0' | wc -l` = 784, of an 821-line span) with **75 branch
statements** (`if`/`elif`/`for`/`while`/`try`/`except` inside 1672–2492) and
**23 route handlers declared inline** (`@app.get`/`@app.post` decorators between
1672 and 2492, e.g. `/healthz` at `http_service.py:1693`, `/portal` at `:1721`,
`POST /portal/draft` at `:1749`, `/portal/manager/reviews` at `:1997`,
`POST /portal/manager/reviews/{review_id}/decision` at `:2060`, and
`GET /api/planner/policy-snapshot` at `:2330`). The factory builds the app object,
configures auth/runtime, and defines every portal, manager, admin, artifact, and
planner-API route as nested closures in one body.

Missing/wrong behavior: there is no module or function boundary between unrelated
route groups (portal vs. manager-review vs. admin-exception vs. planner-API), so
the entire surface is one untestable-in-isolation unit. A handler cannot be
imported, registered, or unit-routed without instantiating the whole factory, and
any edit to one route group risks the others because they share one closure scope.

This is **latent fragility, not a current break**: the app boots and every route
serves today (the 100 tests in `tests/python/test_http_service.py` pass on
`main`). The defect is structural — the function is past any reviewable/atomic
size and there is no seam to register a route group independently, so the next
route addition compounds the same closure.

## Scope

Decompose `create_app` into a thin app factory plus per-group route-registration
helpers. Each helper takes the `FastAPI` app (and the shared runtime/auth
dependencies already constructed in `create_app`) and registers one cohesive
route group. Concretely: `register_portal_routes`, `register_review_routes`,
`register_manager_routes`, `register_admin_routes`, `register_artifact_routes`,
and `register_planner_api_routes`, called in sequence at the end of `create_app`.
The factory keeps app construction, runtime-config load, and auth wiring; route
bodies move verbatim into the helpers. Routing paths, methods, response models,
and auth dependencies are unchanged.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change any route path, HTTP method, `response_model`, `response_class`,
  status code, or auth dependency. This is a structural move, not a behavior
  change; `GET /api/planner/policy-snapshot` and all 22 other routes keep their
  current contracts.
- Do NOT rename or alter the `main`/argument-parser code at `http_service.py:2493+`
  or the `build_arg_parser` block ending at `:2490`.
- Do NOT touch the planner conversation service (`planner.py`) or the frontend —
  those are separate issues; fence them out.
- Scaffold-only / partial completion does NOT count for THIS issue: adding empty
  `register_*` helper stubs, or defining the helpers but leaving the route bodies
  still inline in `create_app` (i.e. `create_app` is not reduced and the 23
  `@app.*` decorators still live between 1672 and the factory's `return app`), is
  a failure. The deliberate-break gate below must be demonstrated, and after the
  move `create_app` must contain 0 inline `@app.` route decorators.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py`, add a
  `register_planner_api_routes(app, <runtime/auth deps>)` helper and move the
  planner-API handlers — `GET /api/planner/policy-snapshot` (`:2330`), the
  submission-status route, and the evaluation route group (decorators at `:2374`,
  `:2402`, `:2441`) — into it verbatim, including their auth dependencies.
- [ ] Add `register_portal_routes(app, ...)` and move the portal-facing handlers:
  `/healthz` (`:1693`), `/portal/demo` (`:1697`), `/portal` (`:1721`),
  `/portal/expenses/new` (`:1733`), `/portal/draft/new` (`:1741`),
  `POST /portal/draft` (`:1749`), `POST /portal/expenses/review` (`:1772`).
- [ ] Add `register_review_routes(app, ...)` and move the draft-review handlers:
  the review-detail GETs at `:1794`/`:1836`,
  `POST /portal/review/{draft_id}/exceptions` (`:1857`),
  `POST /portal/review/{draft_id}/submit` (`:1932`).
- [ ] Add `register_manager_routes(app, ...)` and move
  `/portal/manager/reviews` (`:1997`), the manager-review GET at `:2020`, and
  `POST /portal/manager/reviews/{review_id}/decision` (`:2060`).
- [ ] Add `register_admin_routes(app, ...)` and move
  `POST /portal/admin/exceptions/{draft_id}/{exception_index}/decision` (`:2136`).
- [ ] Add `register_artifact_routes(app, ...)` and move the artifact GETs at
  `:2185`, `/portal/review/{draft_id}/artifacts/{artifact_name}` (`:2220`),
  `/portal/expenses/{draft_id}/artifacts/{artifact_name}` (`:2275`), and the GET
  at `:2319`.
- [ ] Reduce `create_app` (`http_service.py:1672`) to: build `FastAPI` app, load
  runtime config + wire auth, then call the six `register_*` helpers and
  `return app`. Confirm 0 `@app.` route decorators remain inside the body between
  `def create_app` and its `return app`.
- [ ] Perform the deliberate-break verification (see Acceptance Criteria), capture
  the FAIL output, then revert the break before requesting review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Named test: `python -m pytest tests/python/test_http_service.py -q` reports
  0 failed — the full 100-test http_service suite passes unchanged after the move
  (route contracts preserved). In particular
  `test_http_service.py::test_snapshot_route_returns_planner_contract`
  (`tests/python/test_http_service.py:289`) passes (`GET /api/planner/policy-snapshot`
  → 200 with `payload["auth"]["endpoint"] == "GET /api/planner/policy-snapshot"`).
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** in `register_planner_api_routes`, temporarily
  delete the registration of `GET /api/planner/policy-snapshot` (drop the moved
  `@app.get("/api/planner/policy-snapshot", ...)` handler). With that change,
  `python -m pytest tests/python/test_http_service.py -q -k
  test_snapshot_route_returns_planner_contract` **must FAIL** (the route is
  unregistered → response status 404, not 200). Revert the deletion; the test
  passes again. Capture both runs.
- [ ] Structural gate (observable, grep-based): after the move,
  `python - <<'PY'` that reads `http_service.py`, slices the `create_app` body
  (`def create_app` through its `return app`), and counts `@app.` decorators
  returns **0**; equivalently `awk` the 1672→return-app span and
  `grep -cE '@app\.(get|post|put|delete|patch|websocket|api_route)'` returns `0`.
  All 23 decorators now live inside the six `register_*` helpers
  (`grep -cE '@app\.(get|post|put|delete|patch)'` across the helper bodies = 23).
- [ ] `create_app` body shrinks: the line span from `def create_app`
  (`http_service.py:1672`) to its `return app` is < 120 non-blank lines (down from
  784), measured by `awk`/`wc -l` over that slice.
- [ ] Live gate: `tpp-planner-smoke` passes against a running local planner
  service (the same command CI runs at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:189` and
  `.github/workflows/pr-00-gate.yml:234`), confirming the planner-API route group
  still serves end-to-end after relocation.

## Implementation Notes

- Move route bodies verbatim — do not rewrite handler logic — so behavior is
  byte-equivalent; only the enclosing function/registration changes.
- The shared dependencies built once in `create_app` (runtime config, auth
  config/dependency, proposal store) must be passed into each `register_*` helper
  rather than reconstructed, to keep one source of truth.
- Confirmed against current `main`: `http_service.py:1672`
  (`def create_app(store: PlannerProposalStore | None = None) -> FastAPI:`),
  next top-level `def main` at `:2493`, 23 inline `@app.*` decorators between
  1672–2492, 784 non-blank body lines, 75 branch statements;
  `tests/python/test_http_service.py:289`
  (`def test_snapshot_route_returns_planner_contract`) asserts the 200 contract.
- Confirmed-green local reproduction (from repo root, venv active):
  `python -m pytest tests/python/test_http_service.py -q` passes today (100
  tests). Run `tpp-planner-smoke --base-url "$TPP_BASE_URL"` against a local
  service for the live gate (see `docs/deployment.md:101`).
title: Split the 799-line create_app god-function in http_service.py

# Share TPP YAML config-loader and snapshot-store base classes

## Why

The four config-bearing engines each re-implement the same YAML-loading
boilerplate instead of sharing it. `from_environment` is **byte-identical** in
two files — `approval.py:81-87` and `validation.py:312-318` both read
`content = os.getenv(env_var)`, raise `ValueError(f"Environment variable
'{env_var}' is not set or empty")` on empty, then `return cls.from_yaml(content)`.
`from_yaml` repeats the `data = yaml.safe_load(content) or {}` -> `data.get(...)`
-> `raise ValueError("... must include a '...' list")` shape across
`approval.py:56-63`, `validation.py:297-302`, and `providers.py:108-116`.
`from_file` repeats "resolve default path (or package-resource fallback) ->
`target_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` -> `cls.from_yaml(content)`" in all
four: `policy.py:462-467`, `providers.py:118-123`, `approval.py:66-78`,
`validation.py:305-310`. `_load_rules` is a near-twin free function in
`approval.py:23` and `validation.py:275`.

The same kind of copy lives in the SQL persistence backends. `sqlite_store.py`
and `postgres_store.py` each carry a lazy-cache `_connection`
(`sqlite_store.py:68`, `postgres_store.py:62`) and a `save_snapshot`
(`sqlite_store.py:110`, `postgres_store.py:104`) that runs the **same
namespace-reconciliation algorithm** — iterate `snapshot.items()`, branch on
`namespace in RECORD_NAMESPACES and isinstance(value, dict)`, delete rows whose
`record_key` is absent from the incoming namespace, upsert the rest, else write a
singleton blob — differing only in SQL dialect. `load_snapshot`
(`sqlite_store.py:92`, `postgres_store.py:86`) likewise rebuilds the snapshot dict
identically. (`persistence/store.py:21` is already the `PortalStateStore`
`Protocol`; the duplication is in the two concrete SQL implementers, not the
protocol.)

Missing behavior: there is no shared loader helper and no shared SQL-reconcile
base, so a fix to one path (e.g. tightening the empty-YAML `or {}` handling, or
correcting the delete-absent reconcile) silently does not propagate to its twin.
This is **latent fragility, not a current break** — every loader and both stores
work today; the defect is that the duplicated logic can drift between copies and
already has a near-identical-twin maintenance burden.

## Scope

(1) Add a config-loader mixin/base in
`src/travel_plan_permission/config_loader.py` exposing the shared
`from_file`/`from_environment` orchestration and a `_load_yaml_mapping(content,
required_key)` helper; have `PolicyEngine`, `ProviderRegistry`, `ApprovalEngine`,
and `PolicyValidator` consume it so each retains only its rule-construction
specifics. (2) Add a `SqlSnapshotStore` abstract base in
`src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sql_store.py` that holds the
namespace-reconciliation control flow of `save_snapshot`/`load_snapshot` and
delegates dialect-specific statements (delete-absent, upsert-record,
upsert-singleton, select-all) to abstract methods; have `SQLitePortalStateStore`
and `PostgresPortalStateStore` subclass it. Python package only;
`config/*.yaml`, the `RECORD_NAMESPACES` tuple, the HTTP service, and the JSON
backend are untouched.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change any public method signature or return type: `from_yaml(content)`,
  `from_file(path=None)`, `from_environment(env_var=...)`, `initialize()`,
  `load_snapshot() -> dict|None`, and `save_snapshot(snapshot)` keep their current
  signatures and observable behavior (same `ValueError` messages, same
  `FileNotFoundError` text).
- Do NOT touch `persistence/json_store.py` (`JsonPortalStateStore`) — it writes a
  single-blob file and is intentionally not part of the SQL-reconcile family.
- Do NOT add or remove entries from `RECORD_NAMESPACES`
  (`persistence/store.py:11`) or change the `PortalStateStore` Protocol surface.
- Do NOT introduce a new YAML schema, rename config keys, or alter
  `config/policy.yaml` / `config/providers.yaml`.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding `config_loader.py` /
  `sql_store.py` while the four engines still inline their own `from_file`/
  `from_environment` bodies, or while `SQLitePortalStateStore.save_snapshot`
  (`sqlite_store.py:110`) and `PostgresPortalStateStore.save_snapshot`
  (`postgres_store.py:104`) still carry their own reconcile loops, is a failure of
  THIS issue. The deliberate-break gates below must be demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] Create `src/travel_plan_permission/config_loader.py` with a
  `YamlConfigLoaderMixin` providing classmethods `from_file(cls, path=None)` and
  `from_environment(cls, env_var)` plus a static `_load_yaml_mapping(content,
  required_key=None)`, lifting the byte-identical `from_environment` body from
  `approval.py:81-87` / `validation.py:312-318` verbatim.
- [ ] Refactor `ApprovalEngine` (`approval.py:56-87`) and `PolicyValidator`
  (`validation.py:297-318`) to inherit `from_environment`/`from_file` from
  `YamlConfigLoaderMixin`, keeping each `from_yaml` calling
  `_load_yaml_mapping(content, "rules")` then its own `_load_rules(...)`; remove
  the now-redundant inline `os.getenv`/`yaml.safe_load(content) or {}` bodies.
- [ ] Refactor `ProviderRegistry.from_file`/`from_yaml` (`providers.py:108-123`)
  and `PolicyEngine.from_yaml`/`from_file` (`policy.py:374,462`) onto the shared
  `from_file` orchestration + `_load_yaml_mapping`, preserving
  `PolicyEngine.from_yaml`'s `_load_rule_config` rule assembly and
  `ProviderRegistry`'s `model_validate(data)` path.
- [ ] Collapse the twin free functions `_load_rules` in `approval.py:23` and
  `validation.py:275` into one parametrized helper (e.g. in `config_loader.py`
  taking a per-rule factory), and call it from both modules.
- [ ] Create `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sql_store.py` with an
  abstract `SqlSnapshotStore` that implements the `save_snapshot`/`load_snapshot`
  namespace-reconciliation control flow once (the loop over `snapshot.items()`
  and the `namespace in RECORD_NAMESPACES and isinstance(value, dict)` branch),
  delegating to abstract `_delete_absent_records`, `_upsert_record`,
  `_upsert_singleton`, and `_select_all` methods.
- [ ] Subclass `SqlSnapshotStore` from `SQLitePortalStateStore`
  (`sqlite_store.py:110` reconcile loop) and `PostgresPortalStateStore`
  (`postgres_store.py:104` reconcile loop), so each keeps only its `_connection`
  (`sqlite_store.py:68`, `postgres_store.py:62`) and its dialect-specific SQL in
  the delegated methods; remove the duplicated reconcile loops.
- [ ] Perform the two deliberate-break verifications (see Acceptance Criteria),
  capture the FAIL output for each, then revert both breaks before requesting
  review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Named loader tests pass post-refactor:
  `python -m pytest tests/python/test_approval_engine.py::test_load_rules_from_environment
  tests/python/test_providers.py::test_lookup_filters_by_destination_and_validity
  tests/python/test_validation.py -q` reports 0 failures.
- [ ] Named persistence test passes post-refactor:
  `python -m pytest "tests/python/test_portal_state_store.py::TestSQLitePortalStateStore::test_save_snapshot_reconciles_absent_records"
  -q` reports 0 failures.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate A (loader):** in the shared
  `_load_yaml_mapping` helper, temporarily return `{}` instead of the parsed
  mapping (drop the `data.get(required_key)` result). With that change,
  `tests/python/test_approval_engine.py::test_load_rules_from_environment`
  **must FAIL** (no rules load -> the empty-rules `ValueError` or an empty engine).
  Revert; the test passes. Capture both runs.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate B (persistence):** in `SqlSnapshotStore`'s shared
  reconcile flow, temporarily skip the delete-absent step (comment out the
  `_delete_absent_records` call). With that change,
  `tests/python/test_portal_state_store.py::TestSQLitePortalStateStore::test_save_snapshot_reconciles_absent_records`
  **must FAIL** (a record absent from the new snapshot survives, so the asserted
  reconciled keys do not match). Revert; the test passes. Capture both runs.
- [ ] Dedup is observable (grep-based): after the refactor,
  `grep -rc 'content = os.getenv(env_var)' src/travel_plan_permission/approval.py
  src/travel_plan_permission/validation.py` returns `0` for both files (the body
  now lives only in `config_loader.py`), and
  `grep -c 'isinstance(value, dict)' src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sqlite_store.py
  src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/postgres_store.py` returns `0` for both
  (the reconcile branch now lives only in `sql_store.py`).
- [ ] Full-suite regression gate: `python -m pytest tests/python -q` reports 0
  failures (the Postgres backend tests in `TestPostgresPortalStateStore` skip or
  pass per their existing driver guard, unchanged by this refactor).

## Implementation Notes

- Lift, don't rewrite: move the `from_environment` body and the
  `yaml.safe_load(content) or {}` + required-key `ValueError` shape into
  `config_loader.py` so the messages stay string-identical (the loader tests
  assert on behavior, and `from_environment`'s message is verbatim-shared today).
- `persistence/store.py:11` `RECORD_NAMESPACES` and the `PortalStateStore`
  Protocol (`:21`) are the existing seam the new `SqlSnapshotStore` plugs into;
  keep the base implementing that Protocol so the resolver
  (`TestResolver` in `test_portal_state_store.py`) still type-checks.
- All cited symbols/lines confirmed against current `origin/main` via
  `git show origin/main:<path> | grep -nE ...`: identical `from_environment`
  (`approval.py:81`, `validation.py:312`), `from_yaml`/`from_file` family
  (`policy.py:374,462`; `providers.py:108,118`; `approval.py:56,66`;
  `validation.py:297,305`), twin `_load_rules` (`approval.py:23`,
  `validation.py:275`), parallel `_connection`/`save_snapshot`/`load_snapshot`
  (`sqlite_store.py:68,110,92`; `postgres_store.py:62,104,86`).
- Confirmed-green local reproduction (from repo root, venv active; pytest
  `testpaths = ["tests"]` per `pyproject.toml:88`):
  `python -m pytest tests/python/test_approval_engine.py tests/python/test_providers.py tests/python/test_validation.py "tests/python/test_portal_state_store.py::TestSQLitePortalStateStore" -q`
  passes today.
title: Share TPP YAML config-loader and snapshot-store base classes

body:
**Why**: `render.yaml` sets `TPP_PORTAL_STATE_PATH=/tmp/tpp/portal-runtime-state.sqlite3` (line 37), and `docs/deployment.md:12-13` confirms "portal and proposal state is disposable across restarts and redeploys." On the free tier the service spins down after inactivity (`docs/deployment.md:10`), so anything a tester submits through the live portal can silently vanish mid-session. This directly undercuts the persistence story the README advertises — including its own restart-verification instruction to "create a draft, copy the `/portal/review/{draft_id}` URL, restart the service, and reopen the same page" (`README.md:151-156`). The durable backend already exists and is resolver-selected, so this is a config + UX gap, not missing code.

**Scope**: Either point the hosted deployment's portal state at a durable store, or render an explicit "demo state is not retained" notice on the portal home so testers are not misled. Keep within the privacy constraint: a durable store, if added, must be in-perimeter / org-controlled, not a community SaaS database holding real data.

**Non-Goals**:
- Do NOT mandate a paid Postgres tier or make durability a hard requirement for the synthetic demo.
- Not done if only docs change: either `render.yaml` stops pointing durable user state at `/tmp` **or** the portal home template shows the ephemerality notice — a prose-only edit does not satisfy this.

**Tasks**:
- [ ] In `render.yaml`, either set `TPP_PORTAL_DATABASE_URL` to an org-controlled/managed Postgres (the `postgres` extra and `psycopg[binary]` are already declared in `pyproject.toml`; resolver routes to Postgres when this env is set — `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/resolver.py:45`), or move `TPP_PORTAL_STATE_PATH` off `/tmp` to a persistent disk path.

**Why**: `docs/ORCHESTRATION_PLAN.md:363` states "LLM agents are implemented as node functions in the orchestrator," but no LLM call code exists in `src/`: a grep for `ChatOpenAI|langchain_openai|import openai|openai\.` over `src/` returns **nothing**. A coding agent or reviewer picking up this repo will assume capabilities that do not exist — a readiness-misleading doc-drift gap. This is documentation only, but it directly contradicts the README's accurate "intentionally small and server-rendered ... deterministic" framing (`README.md:133-136`).

**Scope**: Make `docs/ORCHESTRATION_PLAN.md` state plainly which phases are built (deterministic policy/planner-runtime/spreadsheet seam) versus aspirational (LLM agents, vendor/travel-API search, receipt-OCR-in-graph), and correct the "agents are implemented" sentence. Add a machine-checkable status marker so the drift cannot silently reopen.

**Non-Goals**:
- Do NOT implement the agents, vendor search, or wire OCR into the graph.
- Not done if a status section is added but the false "LLM agents are implemented" sentence at `docs/ORCHESTRATION_PLAN.md:363` is left intact — that exact claim must be corrected.

**Tasks**:

body:
**Why**: The product's value is the end-to-end approval loop, but a non-developer on a locked-down work PC (no install, no terminal) cannot see it today. The only browser-reachable surface is the public Render free-tier deployment, which exposes only the *unauthenticated* traveler forms — `portal_home` (`src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:1641`), `portal_draft_form` (`:1660`), and `portal_expense_form` (`:1652`) take a bare `Request` with no auth. The reviewer/admin surfaces are gated: `portal_manager_review_queue` (`:1916`) and `portal_manager_review_detail` (`:1944`) both call `_authorize_request(..., required_permission=Permission.VIEW)` (helper at `:359`), so they return 401 with no seeded session, and the admin/exception decision routes (`:2055`, `portal_admin_dashboard` at `:2109`) are likewise gated. There is no documented no-terminal walkthrough: a repo-wide grep for `no-install|no-terminal|streamlit|codespace|devcontainer|stlite|pyodide` matches only incidental planning text in `docs/IMMEDIATE_ACTION_PLAN.md` / `docs/DEPENDABOT_PR_ANALYSIS.md`, never a hosted demo runbook (`docs/demo-script.md` is an aspirational Excel-agent narrative, not a click-through). The Render path is also fragile: `docs/deployment.md:10-13` documents ~50s cold-start and disposable `/tmp` state, and there is no scheduled liveness probe, so it can be silently down. **Privacy constraint**: the org cannot place proprietary travel/expense data on community/external SaaS, so the *public* demo must run on synthetic fixtures only, and the real-data path must be a deterministic, in-perimeter deployment with the (currently nonexistent) LLM features kept out of the proprietary zone.

**Scope**: Two grounded outcomes. (1) A **synthetic-only** browser demo of the complete loop — traveler form → manager review queue → admin/exception decision — reachable with no terminal, seeded exclusively from repo fixtures, plus a guarded way to mint/seed a demo reviewer session. (2) A documented **internal/on-prem hosting runbook** for the real-data zone (data stays in the org perimeter) and a scheduled liveness check so a down demo is visible.

**Non-Goals**:
- Do NOT implement the LLM agents or vendor search (separate effort; see the doc-drift issue below) — and do NOT route any real travel/expense data to an external LLM.
- Do NOT put proprietary data on Streamlit Community Cloud, public HF Spaces, or any community SaaS; the public demo is synthetic-fixtures-only.
- Not done if the only deliverable is README prose: a reviewer must be able to actually open a *populated* `/portal/manager/reviews` page without a terminal, and the seed must come from fixtures (no hand-typed real data). Scaffold-only (e.g. an env flag that exists but seeds nothing) does not satisfy this.

**Tasks**:
- [ ] Add a guarded `TPP_DEMO_MODE` boot path in `create_app` (`src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py`) that, when set, seeds the `proposal_store` from repo fixtures — call `proposal_store.save_portal_draft(...)` and `proposal_store.create_manager_review(...)` (defined at `http_service.py:560` and `:704`) using `tests/fixtures/canonical_trip_plan_realistic.json` and `tests/fixtures/sample_expense_report_minimal.json`. Default OFF.
- [ ] In `TPP_DEMO_MODE`, mint and surface a demo reviewer bearer token via `mint_bootstrap_token` (`src/travel_plan_permission/planner_auth.py:260`) so the auth-gated `portal_manager_review_queue` (`http_service.py:1916`) is reachable; document pasting it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or wire a demo-only cookie the gated routes accept.
- [ ] Add a `docs/no-terminal-demo.md` runbook: (a) the **synthetic** public demo (Render or equivalent) with the cold-start caveat from `docs/deployment.md:10-11`, and (b) an **internal/on-prem** option (internal container host / Posit Connect / internal Azure web app) for the real-data zone, explicitly stating data never leaves the perimeter and the LLM-dependent features are disabled in that zone.
- [ ] Add a scheduled liveness workflow `.github/workflows/maint-render-liveness.yml` (cron, modeled on the existing scheduled workflows in `.github/workflows/`) that runs `tpp-planner-smoke --base-url <synthetic-demo-url>` — the `--base-url` flag exists (`src/travel_plan_permission/planner_smoke.py:47`) and `_validate_readyz` hits `/readyz` (`:203`) — and fails (surfacing a red run) when the demo is down.
- [ ] Set `render.yaml` env so the public service is unambiguously synthetic: add `TPP_DEMO_MODE=1` and keep no real `TPP_ACCESS_TOKEN` wired to proprietary backends; add a code comment that this deployment is fixtures-only.
- [ ] Link the new runbook from `README.md` under "Documentation" (`README.md:185-191`) and add a one-line "Try it in a browser (synthetic data only)" pointer near the Planner HTTP Service section (`README.md:49-53`).

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] New test `tests/test_http_service.py::test_demo_mode_seeds_reviewable_queue` (failing today) boots the app with `TPP_DEMO_MODE=1`, requests `/portal/manager/reviews` with the demo token, and asserts HTTP 200 with at least one seeded review row rendered — and asserts the same route returns 401 when `TPP_DEMO_MODE` is unset (proving the gate still holds for the proprietary zone).
- [ ] New test asserts the demo seed values originate from `tests/fixtures/*.json` (e.g. a fixture-derived traveler name appears in the rendered queue), proving zero real data is embedded.
- [ ] The scheduled liveness workflow exists and, on a manual `workflow_dispatch`, runs `tpp-planner-smoke --base-url` against the synthetic demo URL and reports pass/fail in the Actions log.
- [ ] `docs/no-terminal-demo.md` exists and contains both a synthetic-public section and an internal/on-prem section that states real data stays in-perimeter and LLM features are disabled there; a reviewer following it cold reaches a populated `/portal/manager/reviews` page without running a terminal command.

**Implementation Notes**: Reviewer/admin gating lives in `http_service.py` at `:1916`, `:1944`, `:2055`, `:2109`; the auth helper is `_authorize_request` (`:359`) wrapping `authenticate_request`. Store seam methods: `save_portal_draft` (`:560`), `cache_portal_artifacts` (`:586`), `create_manager_review` (`:704`), `apply_manager_review_action` (`:746`). Token minting: `mint_bootstrap_token` (`planner_auth.py:260`), CLI entry `tpp-planner-token` (`pyproject.toml` scripts → `planner_auth:main`). Keep `TPP_DEMO_MODE` strictly opt-in and never auto-enabled when `TPP_PORTAL_DATABASE_URL` points at a real Postgres. Note this app is FastAPI + uvicorn + SQL + OIDC (`pyproject.toml` deps), so it **cannot** run as stlite/Pyodide in-browser — the synthetic public demo must be a server deployment fed fixtures, and the proprietary path must be internal browser-accessible hosting, not client-side WASM.
