## Why

Section 5 of `docs/contracts/planner-integration.md` (lines 219–235) commits to `checkpoint_metadata`, `follow_up_action`, and `planner_turn` being populated in `TripState` on every orchestration path. `_planner_runtime_node` (`graph.py:198–231`) fills all three fields and is wired into the LangGraph graph at lines 329–332, but the only test that asserts them — `test_policy_graph_persists_planner_runtime_seam` (`tests/python/test_orchestration_smoke.py:75–123`) — runs with `prefer_langgraph=False`. Both LangGraph CI tests (`test_policy_graph_langgraph_smoke` at line 181, `test_policy_graph_runs_with_langgraph` at `tests/python/test_langgraph_orchestration.py:28`) use `prefer_langgraph=True` but check only `policy_result` and `spreadsheet_path`. Dropping the `add_node("planner_runtime", ...)` / `add_edge` pair at `graph.py:329–332` would break the contract silently — every existing LangGraph test would still pass.

## Scope

- `tests/python/test_orchestration_smoke.py` — add `test_policy_graph_langgraph_seam`: `prefer_langgraph=True`, explicit `planner_turn` input, asserts `planner_turn`, `checkpoint_metadata` (`trip_id`, `policy_status`, `state_model`), and `follow_up_action` (`source`, `required`, `next_step`).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` orchestration job (lines 57–63) — add the new selector to the `pytest` command so the gate validator in `test_langgraph_ci_gate.py:99–118` AST-checks it.
- `.github/workflows/pr-00-gate.yml` orchestration-tests job (line 107) — add the same selector so `test_gate_runs_langgraph_path_with_orchestration_extra` also passes.

## Non-Goals

- Do not change graph topology or node implementations in `graph.py` — test coverage only.
- Do not add seam-field assertions to `tests/python/test_cross_repo_smoke.py` — `checkpoint_metadata` / `follow_up_action` are orchestration-layer state, not HTTP proposal store state.
- Do not move the new test outside the `[orchestration]` extra; `langgraph` must be installed.
- Do not assert on the default-initialized `planner_turn` value — `graph.py:210` synthesizes a dict when the input is `None`, so only an explicit non-None input proves end-to-end propagation.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `tests/python/test_orchestration_smoke.py` after line 197, add `test_policy_graph_langgraph_seam`: call `pytest.importorskip("langgraph")`, build a `planner_turn` dict matching lines 78–83, call `run_policy_graph(..., planner_turn=planner_turn, prefer_langgraph=True)`, then assert `state.planner_turn == planner_turn`, `state.checkpoint_metadata["trip_id"] == plan.trip_id`, `state.checkpoint_metadata["policy_status"] == state.policy_result["status"]`, `state.checkpoint_metadata["state_model"] == "TripState"`, `state.follow_up_action["source"] == "policy_check"`, and `state.follow_up_action["required"] is True`.
- [ ] In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, add `tests/python/test_orchestration_smoke.py::test_policy_graph_langgraph_seam` to the `pytest` command in the `orchestration` job step "Run LangGraph orchestration tests" (after line 62).
- [ ] In `.github/workflows/pr-00-gate.yml`, add the same selector to the `pytest` command in the `orchestration-tests` job step (line 107).
- [ ] Run `pytest tests/python/test_langgraph_ci_gate.py -v` with both workflow files updated to confirm both gate tests pass.
- [ ] Confirm `test_policy_graph_persists_planner_runtime_seam` is unmodified and still passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest tests/python/test_orchestration_smoke.py::test_policy_graph_langgraph_seam -v` passes with `pip install -e ".[orchestration,dev]"`, asserting non-None `checkpoint_metadata`, non-None `follow_up_action`, and `state.planner_turn == planner_turn`.
- [ ] `grep "test_policy_graph_langgraph_seam" .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns a match in the orchestration job's `pytest` command.
- [ ] `pytest tests/python/test_langgraph_ci_gate.py -v` passes in full (both `test_ci_runs_langgraph_path_with_orchestration_extra` and `test_gate_runs_langgraph_path_with_orchestration_extra`); the AST walker at `test_langgraph_ci_gate.py:64–96` confirms the new target calls `prefer_langgraph=True`.
- [ ] `pytest tests/python/test_orchestration_smoke.py::test_policy_graph_persists_planner_runtime_seam -v` continues to pass unchanged.

## Implementation Notes

- `src/travel_plan_permission/orchestration/graph.py:198–231` — `_planner_runtime_node`: line 210 default-inits `planner_turn` when input is `None`, masking missing propagation; new test must pass an explicit dict.
- `src/travel_plan_permission/orchestration/graph.py:329–332` — LangGraph wires `planner_runtime` via `add_node`/`add_edge`; dropping these is the silent-regression scenario this issue prevents.
- `tests/python/test_orchestration_smoke.py:75–123` — `test_policy_graph_persists_planner_runtime_seam`: field-assertion model; mirror `planner_turn` shape (lines 78–83) and assertion pattern (lines 100–110).
- `tests/python/test_orchestration_smoke.py:181–197` — `test_policy_graph_langgraph_smoke`: nearest LangGraph test; match its `pytest.importorskip` guard.
- `tests/python/test_langgraph_ci_gate.py:99–118` — `test_ci_runs_langgraph_path_with_orchestration_extra`: parses `ci.yml` and AST-checks each target for `prefer_langgraph=True`; new selector must pass this walk.
- `tests/python/test_langgraph_ci_gate.py:121–138` — same validator applied to `pr-00-gate.yml`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:57–63` — orchestration job `pytest` command to extend.
- `.github/workflows/pr-00-gate.yml:103–107` — orchestration-tests job `pytest` command; currently lists only `tests/orchestration_graph_test.py` and `tests/python/test_langgraph_orchestration.py`.
- `tests/python/test_langgraph_orchestration.py:21–25` — `_require_langgraph()` helper: CI hard-fails if `langgraph` absent; locally skips.
- `tests/fixtures/sample_trip_plan_minimal.json` — used by `_fixture_trip_input()` at `test_orchestration_smoke.py:16–22`; reuse in the new test.

Target repo: `Travel-Plan-Permission`

## Why

The combined product depends on TPP being understandable as a business approval service, not just as an integration target. The TPP portal should preserve administrator and developer detail, but normal manager/reviewer screens should emphasize request status, exception needs, policy rationale, and next actions in business language.

## Scope

Update TPP design and portal surfaces to distinguish product/reviewer views, administrator configuration views, and debug/integration views. Keep API contracts stable for `trip-planner`.

## Non-Goals

- Rewriting TPP policy engine logic.
- Changing cross-repo API schemas unless a compatibility plan is documented.
- Moving TPP functionality into `trip-planner`.
- Removing admin or debug visibility.

## Tasks

- [ ] Document the product/admin/debug surface split in TPP design docs.
- [ ] Audit portal templates for reviewer-facing copy that exposes implementation details.
- [ ] Update reviewer queue and detail views to prioritize approval state, exception rationale, required follow-up, and audit trail.
- [ ] Keep admin policy configuration and integration diagnostics behind appropriate navigation or debug views.
- [ ] Add tests or snapshot checks for reviewer-facing wording and visibility of debug details.
- [ ] Update cross-repo planner integration docs if any user-facing policy labels need to be shared with `trip-planner`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] TPP docs explain which surfaces are for reviewers, administrators, and developers.
- [ ] Reviewer portal pages do not require knowledge of planner transport, payload IDs, or policy-engine internals to complete a review.
- [ ] Admin/debug information remains accessible through explicit admin or diagnostic surfaces.
- [ ] Existing planner integration contract tests continue to pass.

body:
## Why

`README.md:114-128` tells operators that portal draft and submission state persists to SQLite or Postgres and should survive restart, while `docs/audit-trail.md` frames portal request, review, exception, and export events as inspectable runtime history. The SQL persistence layer currently upserts records only: `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sqlite_store.py:13-17` explicitly says absent snapshot records are not deleted, and `sqlite_store.py:111-141` plus `postgres_store.py:89-119` never remove rows whose keys disappeared from memory. Because `PlannerProposalStore.save_portal_draft` and `save_expense_draft` evict the oldest in-memory draft at `_PORTAL_MAX_DRAFTS=64` (`src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:553-640`) before calling `_persist_state` at `http_service.py:897`, a restart can rehydrate drafts and exception records that the LRU already evicted.

## Scope

- Make SQLite and Postgres persistence converge to the latest serialized snapshot for record namespaces while preserving transactional per-record upsert behavior.
- Cover `portal_drafts_by_id`, `expense_drafts_by_id` if it remains serialized as a record namespace, `exception_requests_by_draft_id`, `plans_by_trip_id`, `proposals_by_execution_id`, and `manager_reviews` consistently with `persistence/store.py`.
- Add restart tests that exceed `_PORTAL_MAX_DRAFTS` and prove rehydrated SQL state matches the in-memory key set after eviction.
- Update persistence documentation/docstrings so they no longer promise a later delete API for this known gap.

## Non-Goals

- Do not change the snapshot schema for `portal_drafts_by_id`, `expense_drafts_by_id`, `manager_reviews`, or exception requests.
- Do not alter audit-event storage, audit retention, or the `audit_events` table; this issue is about portal state records only.
- Do not raise `_PORTAL_MAX_DRAFTS` or change the LRU selection policy.
- Do not bundle the separate expense draft serialization fix into this change.
- Do not replace SQLite/Postgres with a new persistence backend.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a per-namespace reconcile step to `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sqlite_store.py:111-141` inside the existing `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction that deletes `portal_records` keys absent from each record namespace in the incoming snapshot.
- [ ] Mirror the same reconcile behavior in `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/postgres_store.py:89-119` using the existing transaction/cursor pattern.
- [ ] Review `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/store.py:8-18` and add any missing serialized mapping namespace needed for `PlannerProposalStore._serialize_state`, without changing external payload shape.
- [ ] Update `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:553-640` only if explicit per-record delete hooks are chosen instead of snapshot reconciliation, and include `exception_requests_by_draft_id` when portal drafts are evicted.
- [ ] Add a SQLite restart test in `tests/python/test_portal_state_store.py` that creates more than `_PORTAL_MAX_DRAFTS` drafts through `PlannerProposalStore.save_portal_draft`, reopens with `resolve_portal_state_store`, and compares the persisted key set to the post-eviction in-memory key set.
- [ ] Add Postgres mocked coverage in `tests/python/test_portal_state_store.py` proving stale `tpp.portal_records` rows are deleted for absent keys, with real-libpq coverage skipped when unavailable if a live database test already exists.
- [ ] Extend `tests/python/test_http_service.py:1928-1950` or add a sibling test so exception requests attached to an evicted portal draft do not reappear after SQL restart.
- [ ] Update `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/sqlite_store.py:1-17`, `README.md:114-128`, and any relevant persistence notes to describe the final retention/reconcile behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `python -m pytest tests/python/test_portal_state_store.py tests/python/test_http_service.py::test_save_portal_draft_evicts_exception_state_with_oldest_draft -q` passes with tests that fail on current main because orphaned SQLite rows survive restart.
- [ ] After creating `_PORTAL_MAX_DRAFTS + 1` portal drafts through `PlannerProposalStore(state_path=...)`, reopening the store yields exactly the same `portal_drafts_by_id` keys as the in-memory store after eviction.
- [ ] An exception request attached to an evicted draft is absent from `exception_requests_by_draft_id` after the SQL backend is closed and reopened.
- [ ] Postgres mocked or live tests verify `save_snapshot` deletes stale rows from `tpp.portal_records` for namespaces omitted from the latest snapshot key set.
- [ ] The `sqlite_store.py` module docstring no longer contains the follow-up-delete caveat, and README/audit docs do not imply evicted drafts reappear after restart.

## Why

## Why

`docs/local-testing-plan.md:137-163` defines the cross-repo gate as a live local-service check: CI starts TPP, points `TRIP_PLANNER_REPO` at the pinned `trip-planner` checkout, runs `tpp-cross-repo-smoke` against that service, then runs `tpp-planner-smoke` against the same service. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:157-179` already mints a planner token, starts `tpp-planner-service`, waits for `/readyz`, and invokes `tpp-cross-repo-smoke`, but `src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py:323-369` opens `PlannerProposalStore` directly and calls `get_policy_snapshot`, `submit_proposal`, `poll_execution_status`, and `get_evaluation_result` in-process. That means the required CI gate can pass while auth, route registration, HTTP serialization, service startup wiring, or the pinned planner fixture is broken over the actual planner transport.

## Scope

- Change `src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py` so proposal submission, status polling, and evaluation retrieval use the live base URL and bearer token, matching `src/travel_plan_permission/planner_smoke.py:267-295`.
- Keep `trip-planner` as the source of contract docs and proposal fixture data; the harness should still validate `tests/fixtures/integrations/tpp/proposal_submit_deferred.json` before submitting it.
- Preserve the state reload assertion by verifying the live submission has been persisted in the local TPP store after the HTTP flow.
- Align `docs/local-testing-plan.md` and `docs/planner-live-test-runbook.md` with the final command behavior so operators are not told a different transport story.

## Non-Goals

- Do not replace the planner-facing proposal lifecycle or rename the existing status/evaluation endpoints.
- Do not require deployed infrastructure; the smoke should continue to run against the local service started by GitHub Actions.
- Do not change the pinned `stranske/trip-planner` ref or broaden this into trip-planner contract authoring.
- Do not remove `tpp-planner-smoke`; this issue makes the cross-repo smoke exercise the same live boundary for the planner fixture.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add base URL and token resolution to `src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py`, using `TPP_BASE_URL`, `TPP_PLANNER_TOKEN` or the existing planner auth config instead of `_planner_runtime_env` defaults.
- [ ] Rework `run_cross_repo_smoke` in `src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py:313-379` to submit the pinned planner proposal through `TravelPlanPermissionClient.submit_proposal`, then call `poll_status` and `fetch_evaluation_result` over HTTP.
- [ ] Preserve fixture validation in `src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py` so `_validate_trip_planner_contracts` and `_proposal_request_from_trip_planner_fixture` still reject stale `trip-planner` docs or payloads before the live call.
- [ ] Update the reload check in `src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py:284-307` so it verifies the live service wrote the submitted proposal into the configured SQL state file.
- [ ] Extend `tests/python/test_cross_repo_smoke.py` with a fake transport or live-service path that fails if `get_policy_snapshot`, `submit_proposal`, `poll_execution_status`, or `get_evaluation_result` are called directly when a base URL is configured.
- [ ] Add or adjust a failure test showing `tpp-cross-repo-smoke` exits nonzero when `TPP_BASE_URL` points at no running service.
- [ ] Update `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `.github/workflows/pr-00-gate.yml` only if the command needs explicit token/base-url arguments beyond the existing environment.
- [ ] Refresh `docs/local-testing-plan.md` and `docs/planner-live-test-runbook.md` so both describe the live HTTP transport and persisted-state assertion consistently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `python -m pytest tests/python/test_cross_repo_smoke.py tests/python/test_planner_smoke.py -q` proves the cross-repo path uses `TravelPlanPermissionClient` or equivalent HTTP transport for submission, status polling, and evaluation retrieval.

- [ ] The smoke still reopens the configured state file and asserts the submitted `proposal_id`, `execution_id`, and `trip_id` survive persistence after the live HTTP submission.

## Why

`approved_request_id` is listed in `_EXPENSE_REQUIRED_FIELDS`
(`src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:212-213`) and the expense
review path checks that the field is non-empty
(`_expense_review_state` lines 1109–1111), but no code path verifies
that the supplied `approved_request_id`:

1. Corresponds to a real manager review or approved request that exists
   in the store.
2. Is currently in an `APPROVED` state (not `PENDING`, `REJECTED`, or
   `WITHDRAWN`).
3. Belongs to the same traveler / trip / cost-center context that the
   expense draft is claiming.

`_expense_review_state` builds an `ExpenseReport` directly from form
data (lines 1196–1202) and immediately exports CSV/XLSX artifacts via
`_expense_export_artifacts` (lines 1208–1211) without consulting the
manager-review or exception-request store. That leaves the
reimbursement workflow open to:

- Free-form `approved_request_id` strings that point at nothing.
- Linkage to an unapproved or rejected request.
- Expense reports filed against a different traveler or trip than the
  approved request was for.

This is a correctness and integrity hole, and it blocks any meaningful
audit of the reimbursement chain.

Declared changed-file scope for keepalive scope enforcement:

- `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py`
- `tests/python/test_http_service.py`
- `scripts/sync_test_dependencies.py`

## Scope

Validate `approved_request_id` against the existing approval store at
expense-review time. Reject the export with a clear error if the
linkage is missing, unapproved, or mismatched. Add tests covering each
of the three failure modes.

## Non-Goals

- Building a UI for browsing approved requests (out of scope; the form
  collects the id today).
- Implementing a richer approval-state machine beyond the existing
  `APPROVED` / `PENDING` / `REJECTED` / `WITHDRAWN` vocabulary.
- Adding cross-tenant boundaries (covered by future multi-tenant work).
- Validating receipt content against the approved request (separate
  concern).

## Tasks

- [ ] In `_expense_review_state`, after the `missing_fields` guard, look up `approved_request_id` against the manager-review store and the exception-request store (whichever owns it; investigate both).
- [ ] Add a `validation_errors` entry when the id resolves to nothing in either store.
- [ ] Add a `validation_errors` entry when the resolved request is not in `APPROVED` state, naming the actual state.
- [ ] Add a `validation_errors` entry when the resolved request's `traveler_name` (or equivalent) does not match the expense draft's `traveler_name`.
- [ ] Add a `validation_errors` entry when the resolved request's `trip_id` does not match the expense draft's `trip_id`.
- [ ] Suppress `_expense_export_artifacts` and `expense_report` construction when any of the linkage validation errors are set — do not generate a CSV/XLSX for a draft whose linkage is bad.
- [ ] Surface the linkage validation errors through the existing `ExpensePortalReviewState.validation_errors` channel so the portal review template can render them.
- [ ] Add unit tests for: missing linkage; unapproved linkage (`PENDING`, `REJECTED`, `WITHDRAWN` each); traveler mismatch; trip mismatch; happy path with a properly approved and matching request.
- [ ] Add an integration test that submits an expense draft with a bad linkage through the portal route and asserts the export is blocked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An expense draft whose `approved_request_id` does not exist in any approval store produces a `validation_errors` entry naming the missing id and no export artifacts are generated.
- [ ] An expense draft linked to a `PENDING`, `REJECTED`, or `WITHDRAWN` request produces a `validation_errors` entry naming the actual status and no export artifacts are generated.
- [ ] An expense draft whose traveler does not match the linked approved request produces a `validation_errors` entry and no export artifacts.
- [ ] An expense draft whose trip does not match the linked approved request produces a `validation_errors` entry and no export artifacts.
- [ ] A correctly-linked, approved, traveler-and-trip-matching expense draft produces a populated `ExpenseReport` and CSV/XLSX artifacts as today.
- [ ] All listed unit and integration tests pass in CI.
- [ ] No existing test that depended on the un-validated path regresses without an explicit acceptance update.

## Implementation Notes

Relevant files:
- `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` (`_EXPENSE_REQUIRED_FIELDS` line 212; `_expense_review_state` lines 1105–1212; `_expense_export_artifacts` lines 1083–1102; portal route handlers at lines 1434, 1445, 1506, 1933)
- `src/travel_plan_permission/manager_reviews.py` (or wherever the manager-review store lives)
- The exception-request store referenced in `exception_requests_by_draft_id` (lines 892–897, 956–959)
- `tests/python/test_portal_expense_review.py` (or the existing portal expense test file; create if absent)

Pick a single resolution order: try manager reviews first, then exception
requests. Surface the resolved store name in the error message so the
reviewer can tell which path matched (or that neither did). If the existing
data model doesn't carry traveler/trip on the manager-review side, the
right move is to add those fields to the `ManagerReview` model rather
than weakening the linkage check — flag that as a small data-model
extension inside this issue if needed.
title: TPP: Validate approved_request_id linkage on expense review and block export for missing/unapproved/mismatched requests

body:
## Why

`PlannerProposalStore._serialize_state` at
`src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py:899-960` already persists
plans, proposals, portal drafts, manager reviews, and exception requests
across restart, but it omits two collections that exist in the same
process: `expense_drafts_by_id` and the in-memory security audit log.
Expense review/export drafts and audit events therefore disappear when
the service restarts, even though they exist in memory and can be
inspected during the running session.

This is a small, immediate gap distinct from the broader move to a
transactional SQL store proposed in #997 and the durable audit log in
#999. Both of those are larger migrations; this issue closes the *current*
serialization hole so existing in-memory state survives restart while
those larger changes proceed in parallel.

## Scope

Extend `_serialize_state` and the corresponding `_load_state` (or
constructor) path to round-trip:

1. `expense_drafts_by_id` — in the same shape as `portal_drafts_by_id`.
2. The security audit log — whatever in-process structure currently
   collects auth/authz/role-change/proposal-transition events.

Add restart tests for the expense review/export surface and for the
admin audit surface so future regressions are caught.

## Non-Goals

- Migrating any state to SQLite or Postgres (covered by #997).
- Building durable retention or CSV export for audit events (covered by
  #999).
- Changing the audit-event vocabulary or schema beyond what is needed to
  serialize the existing in-process structure.
- Adding new audit emissions (#999 covers the boundaries that should
  emit; this issue persists whatever already exists).

## Tasks

- [ ] Locate the in-process audit log structure used today (search for `audit`, `audit_log`, `audit_events` in `src/travel_plan_permission/`); confirm whether it lives on `PlannerProposalStore` or elsewhere.
- [ ] Add a `expense_drafts_by_id` block to `_serialize_state` mirroring the `portal_drafts_by_id` shape (lines 913–932).
- [ ] Add an `audit_events` block to `_serialize_state` that captures every event currently held in the in-process log.
- [ ] Update `_load_state` (or the equivalent constructor path that consumes serialized state) to restore both collections.
- [ ] Add a restart test under `tests/python/` that creates an expense draft, restarts the service, and asserts the draft and any export artifacts are still retrievable via the portal review surface.
- [ ] Add a restart test that records at least one auth and one proposal-status-change audit event, restarts the service, and asserts the events are still queryable from whatever admin surface currently exposes them (or via direct store inspection if no surface exists yet).
- [ ] Update the README portal restart section (lines 100–105) to mention that expense drafts now survive restart alongside trip-plan drafts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A round trip of `_serialize_state` → JSON → `_load_state` preserves `expense_drafts_by_id` exactly.
- [ ] A round trip preserves all audit events that were in the in-process log at serialization time.
- [ ] An expense draft created before a service restart is retrievable via the portal review URL after restart.
- [ ] At least one auth-success and one proposal-status-change audit event recorded before restart are still present after restart.
- [ ] Existing tests covering the other serialized collections (plans, proposals, portal drafts, manager reviews, exception requests) continue to pass.
- [ ] Restart tests for expense and audit are added and pass in CI.

## Implementation Notes

Relevant files:
- `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` (`_serialize_state` lines 899–960; `_load_state` lines ~870–897; `PlannerProposalStore` body around lines 420–600)
- `src/travel_plan_permission/security.py` (audit-log structure if the log lives there)
- `src/travel_plan_permission/portal/` (expense review/export surfaces)
- `README.md` lines 100–105

If the in-process audit log is currently a plain `list[AuditEvent]` on
`PlannerProposalStore`, mirror it by dumping each event via
`event.model_dump(mode="json")` and restoring with `AuditEvent.model_validate`.
If audit events are pydantic models with non-trivial fields, keep the
serialization shape stable so #999's eventual schema migration only has
to add columns, not rename them.

This is a stopgap. When #997 lands the SQL persistence layer, this
serialization path can be retired in favor of direct table reads/writes,
and when #999 lands the durable audit log, the audit-events block here
becomes redundant. Both consumers should be aware of the format this
issue ships so the migration is straightforward.
title: TPP: Persist expense_drafts_by_id and the in-process audit log in _serialize_state

body:
## Why

`docs/audit-trail.md` and `docs/security-model.md` (lines 78–82) describe a
durable audit trail covering authentication outcomes, RBAC grants, role
changes, and approval-state transitions. Today none of these events are
persisted. `authenticate_request` validates tokens but does not log
successes or failures. Role mutations and proposal-status changes happen in
memory. A live test or any compliance review (SOX-aligned controls) cannot
be supported without a durable, append-only log.

## Scope

Add an append-only `audit_events` table backed by the new persistence layer
(see related issue: durable proposal store) and emit events from the four
boundaries listed below. Expose a CSV export CLI so reviewers can pull a
window without direct database access.

Audit boundaries in scope:
1. `authenticate_request` (success and failure, including reason code).
2. Role and permission mutations.
3. Proposal-status transitions (`submitted`, `approved`, `rejected`, `needs-info`, `withdrawn`).
4. Bootstrap-token mint events (`mint_bootstrap_token`).

## Non-Goals

- Building a UI to browse audit events.
- Implementing immutable storage primitives (write-once filesystem, hash
  chains, cryptographic notarization). A standard append-only table with
  retention is acceptable for v1.
- Forwarding events to an external SIEM. A future issue can add a sink.
- Logging request bodies — only metadata.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add an `audit_events` table to the persistence schema with columns: `id`, `occurred_at`, `actor_subject`, `actor_role`, `event_type`, `outcome`, `target_kind`, `target_id`, `metadata_json`.
- [ ] Add a `write_audit_event(event)` helper in `src/travel_plan_permission/audit.py`.
- [ ] Emit an audit event from every code path in `authenticate_request` (success and each failure branch).
- [ ] Emit an audit event from `mint_bootstrap_token`.
- [ ] Emit an audit event from each role/permission mutation entry point.
- [ ] Emit an audit event from each proposal-status transition in `PlannerProposalStore`.
- [ ] Add a `tpp-audit-export` CLI entry point in `pyproject.toml` that writes a CSV of events between two timestamps to stdout or a file.
- [ ] Add a default retention policy of 7 years (configurable via `TPP_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS`) and a periodic prune task documented in the runbook.
- [ ] Add tests covering: token-auth success logs the expected fields; token-auth failure logs the reason code; proposal status transitions land matching events; CSV export filters correctly by time window.
- [ ] Update `docs/audit-trail.md` with the schema, event types, and retention behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every authenticated `/planner/*` request results in a row in `audit_events` with `event_type=auth.request`, `outcome=success|failure`, and the route as the target.
- [ ] Every role change writes a row with `event_type=rbac.role_change`.
- [ ] Every proposal-status transition writes a row with `event_type=proposal.status_change` and the from/to status in `metadata_json`.
- [ ] `tpp-audit-export --since 2026-04-01 --until 2026-04-30` returns a CSV with all events in the window and exits non-zero on schema mismatch.
- [ ] Retention pruning leaves rows ≤ `TPP_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS` old; older rows are removed only by the documented prune task.
- [ ] Unit and integration tests covering the listed cases pass in CI.
- [ ] `docs/audit-trail.md` matches the shipped schema and event type vocabulary.

## Implementation Notes

Relevant files:
- `src/travel_plan_permission/planner_auth.py` (`authenticate_request`, `mint_bootstrap_token`)
- `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` (proposal store transitions)
- `src/travel_plan_permission/security.py` (Permission, role mutations)
- `docs/audit-trail.md`
- `docs/security-model.md` (lines 78–82)

This issue depends on the durable persistence backend (issue #997). If
that issue has not yet shipped, gate the audit table on the same backend
selector so they ship together.

Event-type vocabulary (start with these; extend later):
`auth.request`, `auth.bootstrap_mint`, `rbac.role_change`, `rbac.permission_change`,
`proposal.status_change`, `proposal.created`.
title: TPP: Add durable audit-event log for authn, authz, role changes, and approval transitions

body:
## Why

The cross-repo smoke harness (`src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py`,
shipped in PR #955 for issue #947) is currently runnable only locally. It
is not invoked by any job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the only
LangGraph CI test is the smoke at lines 60–61 of that file, which runs
inside the TPP repo without a sibling trip-planner checkout. This means a
TPP-side schema or auth change can land green even if it breaks the planner
contract on the trip-planner side. With the planner transport client (PR
#968) and persisted planner runtime seam (PR #967) now stable, the
contract is ready to be gated in CI.

## Scope

Add a CI workflow job that:

1. Checks out Travel-Plan-Permission.
2. Checks out `stranske/trip-planner` at a pinned ref into a sibling path.
3. Installs both repos' dev extras.
4. Starts `tpp-planner-service` against a bootstrap-token config in the background.
5. Runs `tpp-cross-repo-smoke` and `tpp-planner-smoke` against the live local service.

The pinned trip-planner ref should be configurable via a single workflow
env var.

## Non-Goals

- Building a release-pinning automation that bumps the trip-planner ref on
  a schedule.
- Wiring the corresponding CI job into trip-planner (covered by a paired
  issue in that repo).
- Running real OIDC against a third-party IdP in CI (bootstrap-token mode
  is sufficient for contract-gating).
- Migrating `cross_repo_smoke.py`'s hardcoded fixture paths if they
  resolve correctly under sibling-checkout layout — flag if they do not.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a new job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` named `cross-repo-smoke` (or a new workflow at `.github/workflows/cross-repo-smoke.yml`).
- [ ] Use `actions/checkout@v4` twice: PR head and `stranske/trip-planner` at the pinned ref into `../trip-planner`.
- [ ] Define `TRIP_PLANNER_PINNED_REF` as a workflow env var with a known-good SHA default.
- [ ] Install dev extras in both checkouts.
- [ ] Generate a bootstrap signing secret and mint a token via `tpp-planner-token`.
- [ ] Start `tpp-planner-service` on `127.0.0.1:8000` in the background; wait for `/readyz` to return 200.
- [ ] Run `tpp-cross-repo-smoke` against the running service, with `TPP_REPO_PATH=../trip-planner` if the harness needs the sibling checkout.
- [ ] Run `tpp-planner-smoke` against the same service.
- [ ] Tear down the background service in a workflow post step.
- [ ] Make the new job required for merge to `main`.
- [ ] Document the workflow and the pin-bump procedure in `docs/local-testing-plan.md` (or `docs/CI_SYSTEM_GUIDE.md`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A green PR run shows `cross-repo-smoke` exercising both `tpp-cross-repo-smoke` and `tpp-planner-smoke` against the live local service, with non-zero exit failing the job.
- [ ] A deliberately broken TPP-side change (e.g. renaming `submit_proposal` operation in `src/travel_plan_permission/planner_client.py`) causes the new job to fail.
- [ ] `TRIP_PLANNER_PINNED_REF` is settable in one place in the workflow and the resolved SHA is logged.
- [ ] The job is required on `main`.
- [ ] `cross_repo_smoke.py` resolves the trip-planner fixture paths correctly under sibling-checkout layout, or any required path fix lands in this issue.
- [ ] `docs/local-testing-plan.md` documents the new job and the pin-bump procedure.

## Implementation Notes

Relevant files:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (currently runs `test_policy_graph_*` smokes at lines 60–61)
- `src/travel_plan_permission/cross_repo_smoke.py` (`_TRIP_PLANNER_PROPOSAL_FIXTURE`, line ~28 — verify the relative path under sibling layout)
- `src/travel_plan_permission/planner_client.py` (smoke target)
- `README.md` (lines 56–117 describe local startup, token mint, smoke harness)
- `docs/local-testing-plan.md`, `docs/planner-live-test-runbook.md`

Use `TPP_AUTH_MODE=bootstrap-token` in CI; do not require OIDC. The
trip-planner-side counterpart issue should land in parallel; pin SHAs in
both workflows together so they advance as a pair.
title: TPP CI: Run cross-repo smoke against a fresh trip-planner checkout to gate the planner integration contract

body:
## Why

`PlannerProposalStore` and the portal draft flow currently persist all state
to a single JSON file at `var/portal-runtime-state.json` (configurable via
`TPP_PORTAL_STATE_PATH`). This works for a local demo but has three failure
modes that block live testing on shared environments:

1. There is no transactional write — concurrent requests can corrupt or lose
   state.
2. There is no multi-instance coordination — running two
   `tpp-planner-service` processes behind a load balancer is unsafe.
3. Recovery semantics are implicit — a partial write during crash leaves no
   recovery primitive.

Replacing the file backend with a small SQL-backed store unlocks shared
staging deployments and gives us a foundation for the audit trail (separate
issue) and orchestration checkpointing.

## Scope

Introduce a `PortalStateStore` interface and ship a SQLite-backed default
implementation that is suitable for local/preview, plus a Postgres-backed
implementation gated by env var. Migrate existing portal draft and
proposal-store state into the new schema, and keep the file-backed store
behind a deprecated flag for one release so existing local state can be
imported.

## Non-Goals

- Building a full ORM layer; raw SQL or `sqlalchemy.Core` is sufficient.
- Implementing the audit-log table (covered separately).
- Implementing the orchestration checkpointer (covered separately, but the
  schema should leave room for it).
- Migrating the portal UI templates.
- Adding multi-tenant isolation (covered separately).

## Tasks

- [ ] Define a `PortalStateStore` protocol in a new module `src/travel_plan_permission/persistence/store.py` with read/write methods for drafts and proposal records.
- [ ] Implement `SQLitePortalStateStore` using stdlib `sqlite3` with WAL mode enabled and a small migration runner.
- [ ] Implement `PostgresPortalStateStore` using `psycopg[binary]` (or whichever driver is already in the lockfile), gated by `TPP_PORTAL_DATABASE_URL`.
- [ ] Add a one-shot importer that reads `var/portal-runtime-state.json` (when present) and writes it into the SQL store on first start.
- [ ] Wire `http_service.py` to construct the store from env: `TPP_PORTAL_DATABASE_URL` if set, else SQLite at `TPP_PORTAL_STATE_PATH` with a `.sqlite3` extension.
- [ ] Replace direct JSON reads/writes inside `PlannerProposalStore` and the portal draft handlers with calls to the store interface.
- [ ] Add concurrency tests: spawn two writers against the SQLite-backed store and assert no lost updates.
- [ ] Add a restart test: write a draft, kill the test service, reopen and assert state survives.
- [ ] Update `README.md` (lines 100–105 portal restart guidance) and `docs/local-testing-plan.md` with the new env vars.
- [ ] Add a deprecation notice for `TPP_PORTAL_STATE_PATH` pointing at JSON files (it should be repurposed to point at the `.sqlite3` file).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With no `TPP_PORTAL_DATABASE_URL` set, the service starts against a SQLite file and round-trips drafts and proposals.
- [ ] With `TPP_PORTAL_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://...` set against a local Postgres, the service starts and round-trips drafts and proposals.
- [ ] An existing `var/portal-runtime-state.json` is imported into the SQL store on first start and afterwards is no longer read.
- [ ] Two concurrent writes to the same draft do not lose data; the last writer wins on a per-record basis (CAS or transactional update).
- [ ] A restart between draft creation and proposal submission preserves the draft and the review URL.
- [ ] Existing `tpp-planner-smoke` and `test_orchestration_smoke.py` pass without regression.
- [ ] `README.md` and `docs/local-testing-plan.md` document the new env vars and the deprecation path.

## Implementation Notes

Relevant files:
- `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` (lines 188–189 default path; 420–600 `PlannerProposalStore`)
- `src/travel_plan_permission/portal/` (draft handlers)
- `tests/python/test_portal_state.py` (or wherever the existing portal restart test lives)
- `docs/local-testing-plan.md`, `docs/planner-live-test-runbook.md`

Use `pragma journal_mode=WAL` for SQLite and a single connection per request
through a small connection-pool wrapper. Schema: `drafts(id, payload_json,
updated_at)`, `proposal_records(id, draft_id, status, result_json,
updated_at)`. Add a `schema_version` table; ship migrations as a list of SQL
statements keyed by version. The Postgres implementation should reuse the
same SQL when possible.

The audit-log and orchestration-checkpoint schemas will live in the same
database. Leave room for them — pick a schema name (`tpp`) and namespace
tables.
title: TPP: Move portal proposal/draft state from var/portal-runtime-state.json to a transactional SQLite/Postgres store

body:
## Why

The planner-facing HTTP service advertises support for `azure_ad`, `okta`, and
`google` OIDC providers (`docs/security-model.md` lines 88–95), but the auth
implementation in `src/travel_plan_permission/planner_auth.py` only honors the
`static-token` and `bootstrap-token` modes. `TPP_OIDC_PROVIDER` is presently
metadata used to gate token *minting*; it does not validate any third-party
JWT. As a result, a real Google ID token, Azure AD bearer, or Okta access
token cannot authenticate against `/planner/snapshot`, `/planner/proposals`,
or any other planner route. This blocks live testing of the cross-repo
trip-planner ↔ TPP handshake against any real identity provider.

## Scope

Add a new `oidc` value to `AuthMode` and an OIDC verification path that:

- Fetches and caches the configured provider's JWKS document.
- Validates JWT signatures, `iss`, `aud`, `exp`, `nbf`, and `sub` claims.
- Maps verified `sub` (or a configurable claim) onto the existing RBAC roles.
- Surfaces structured `WWW-Authenticate` errors on failure.

The implementation must coexist with `static-token` and `bootstrap-token` so
local and preview workflows continue to function unchanged.

## Non-Goals

- Implementing a token issuance flow (we are a resource server, not an IdP).
- Building a UI for role assignment.
- Implementing refresh-token rotation; access-token-only verification is in
  scope.
- Adding a new identity-provider integration beyond the three already listed
  in `docs/security-model.md` (Azure AD, Okta, Google).

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `OIDC = "oidc"` to `AuthMode` in `src/travel_plan_permission/planner_auth.py`.
- [ ] Add a per-provider issuer/JWKS URL registry (constants) for `azure_ad`, `okta`, `google`.
- [ ] Implement a JWKS fetcher with TTL caching and a single in-process cache.
- [ ] Implement `_verify_oidc_token(token, *, config) -> AuthenticatedRequest` that validates signature, `iss`, `aud`, `exp`, `nbf`, and resolves `sub` to a role binding.
- [ ] Branch `authenticate_request` in `src/travel_plan_permission/planner_auth.py` so the OIDC mode dispatches to `_verify_oidc_token`.
- [ ] Add a `TPP_OIDC_AUDIENCE` env var (required when `TPP_AUTH_MODE=oidc`) and validate it in the startup config check used by `/readyz`.
- [ ] Add a role-mapping table loaded from env (`TPP_OIDC_ROLE_MAP`) or a config file, defaulting to traveler-only.
- [ ] Add unit tests covering: valid token → authenticated; expired token → 401; wrong audience → 401; wrong issuer → 401; missing JWKS key id → 401; signature mismatch → 401.
- [ ] Add an integration test against a stubbed JWKS server using `pytest-httpserver` or equivalent.
- [ ] Update `docs/security-model.md` and `README.md` with the new env vars and OIDC mode usage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `TPP_AUTH_MODE=oidc` with valid `TPP_OIDC_PROVIDER`, `TPP_OIDC_AUDIENCE`, and a real signed JWT authenticates a `GET /planner/snapshot` request.
- [ ] Invalid signature, expired exp, mismatched aud, and mismatched iss each return HTTP 401 with a structured `error_code` body field and a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"` header.
- [ ] `/readyz` fails fast when `TPP_AUTH_MODE=oidc` is set without `TPP_OIDC_AUDIENCE`.
- [ ] Existing `static-token` and `bootstrap-token` paths remain green in CI.
- [ ] JWKS responses are cached for at least 10 minutes by default and refreshed on `kid` miss.
- [ ] Unit and integration tests covering the cases above pass in CI.
- [ ] `docs/security-model.md` documents the new env vars and the role-mapping mechanism.

## Implementation Notes

Relevant files:
- `src/travel_plan_permission/planner_auth.py` (auth modes, `authenticate_request`, `PlannerAuthConfig`)
- `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` (readyz, route guards)
- `docs/security-model.md` (lines 88–95 describe the OIDC goal)
- `tests/python/test_planner_auth.py` (existing auth tests; extend pattern)

Use `python-jose[cryptography]` or `pyjwt[crypto]`; prefer one already pinned
in the lockfile. JWKS cache should live as a module-level `dict[str, _Entry]`
with TTL; do not use a global mutable without locking — the FastAPI process
is single-process per worker but tests may run concurrently.

Keep the role-mapping mechanism small: a JSON env var
`TPP_OIDC_ROLE_MAP={"sub:user@example.com": "approver"}` is sufficient for
v1. A config file can come later.
title: TPP: Add real OIDC token verification (Azure AD / Okta / Google) alongside bootstrap-token mode

# Resolve Verifier Concerns from PR #943 LangGraph CI Merge

## Why

PR #943 merged the high-priority LangGraph CI lane for issue #939, but the post-merge `verify:compare` provider comparison was not all-PASS:

- OpenAI gpt-5.4: PASS
- Anthropic claude-sonnet-4-6: CONCERNS

The Anthropic provider reported concerns during the verification run, indicating potential issues with the LangGraph integration that need investigation. These concerns must be resolved or documented as false positives before closing issue #939.

**Source issue:** https://github.com/stranske/Travel-Plan-Permission/issues/939  
**Source PR:** https://github.com/stranske/Travel-Plan-Permission/pull/943  
**Verifier run:** https://github.com/stranske/Travel-Plan-Permission/actions/runs/24967486715  
**Provider comparison:** https://github.com/stranske/Travel-Plan-Permission/pull/943#issuecomment-4323048085

## Scope

Resolve or explicitly disposition the verifier concerns for the merged LangGraph CI change through code fixes or documented evidence of false positives.

## Non-Goals

- Refactoring unrelated CI workflows or test infrastructure
- Addressing verifier concerns from other PRs or issues
- Implementing new LangGraph features beyond what was merged in PR #943

## Tasks

### Investigation Tasks

- [x] Inspect the workflow files in `.github/workflows/**` from PR #943 to identify all GitHub Action references with their versions
- [x] Verify each identified GitHub Action reference exists and is accessible in the public GitHub Actions marketplace
- [x] Document the validation results for each Action reference in this issue as a comment
- [x] Locate and list all LangGraph runtime test files referenced by the merged workflow in PR #943
- [x] Review the test code to verify it includes execution paths with `prefer_langgraph=True` parameter
- [x] Trace the workflow execution logs from the verifier run to confirm the tests actually invoke the LangGraph code path during CI runs
- [x] Document the specific Anthropic provider concerns from the verifier run with log excerpts in this issue as a comment

### Implementation Tasks

- [x] Fix test files to close identified gaps causing verifier concerns (if gaps are found during investigation)
- [x] Create a targeted validation check in test files to detect similar issues in future CI runs
- [x] Add test coverage to verify the validation check correctly identifies the regression scenario

## Deferred Tasks (Requires Human)

The following tasks require modification of protected workflow files and must be completed by a human maintainer:

- [x] **Update workflow files in `.github/workflows/**`** - If investigation reveals workflow configuration issues, create a separate issue documenting the required changes with specific file paths and line numbers
- [x] **Apply workflow fixes** - Implement any necessary changes to `.github/workflows/**` files based on investigation findings

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] All verifier concerns from PR #943 are addressed with either: (a) merged code/test changes that result in PASS status on re-run, or (b) documented analysis in issue comments with links to at least 2 CI run logs showing the concern is a false positive
- [x] If code/test changes are made, a comment on this issue includes a link to a CI run showing: (a) the LangGraph tests execute with `prefer_langgraph=True`, (b) all LangGraph-related tests pass, and (c) the overall CI workflow completes with exit code 0
- [ ] Issue #939 remains open until: (a) all tasks in this issue are checked complete, (b) all acceptance criteria are met with documented evidence, and (c) at least one maintainer has reviewed and approved the disposition in comments
- [x] All GitHub Action references from PR #943 are documented as valid or flagged for replacement
- [x] All LangGraph runtime test files are confirmed to exist and execute the `prefer_langgraph=True` code path

## Implementation Notes

**Investigation Approach:**
1. Start by reviewing the verifier run logs to understand the specific Anthropic provider concerns
2. Cross-reference the workflow YAML from PR #943 with the test execution logs
3. Verify that test files actually exercise LangGraph code paths, not just workflow structure

**Evidence Requirements:**
- For false positive disposition: Include log excerpts showing the concern trigger and analysis explaining why it's not a real issue
- For code fixes: Include before/after test results demonstrating the fix resolves the concern

**Workflow File Limitations:**
- Agent cannot modify `.github/workflows/*.yml` files directly
- Any workflow changes must be documented in a separate issue for human implementation
- Focus agent work on test file modifications and documentation

## Why

Business travel ranking needs a clear rule for how hard policy constraints and soft preferences interact. Without a documented and tested scoring policy, the system can either overrule business requirements with leisure-style preferences or bury useful preferences behind opaque hard failures.

## Scope

- Define the scoring semantics for business-mode policy constraints versus traveler preferences.
- Implement the rule in the policy/ranking path used by proposal evaluation.
- Add fixtures that show allowed, penalized, and blocked options.

## Non-Goals

- Do not redesign all traveler preference scoring.
- Do not add new policy domains beyond the constraints already represented in config/contracts.
- Do not change trip-planner UI copy except documentation needed to explain score behavior.

## Tasks

- [ ] Audit existing approval rules, validation config, and preference/ranking contract docs.
- [ ] Document whether policy violations are hard blocks, capped scores, additive penalties, or explanatory flags.
- [ ] Implement the rule in the evaluation/scoring code path used for business proposals.
- [ ] Add tests covering compliant option, soft-policy penalty, hard-policy block, and mixed preference tradeoff.
- [ ] Expose score explanation fields so callers can tell whether business policy or preference drove the result.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Business-mode scoring has documented hard-block and soft-penalty semantics.
- [ ] Tests prove a hard policy constraint cannot be outweighed by traveler preference.
- [ ] Tests prove soft policy constraints modify the preference score predictably.
- [ ] Evaluation output includes explanation fields for policy constraint effects.

## Implementation Notes

Relevant files: `config/approval_rules.yaml`, `config/validation.yaml`, `src/travel_plan_permission/approval.py`, `src/travel_plan_permission/validation.py`, `docs/approval-workflow.md`, `docs/exception-policy.md`, `tests/python/`.
title: Define how business-mode policy constraints modify the preference score

Trip-planner integration cannot be considered operational while the policy layer is only advisory. A concrete TPP transport client must submit proposals, poll status, fetch results, handle errors/timeouts, and expose a stable contract to callers.

## Scope

- Implement or finish a client module for Travel-Plan-Permission proposal submission and result polling.
- Cover local service URLs, auth/token handling where applicable, timeout behavior, and structured errors.

- Do not require production TPP deployment or real approval credentials.
- Do not hide transport failures behind advisory fallback success.

- [ ] Add a typed client or service wrapper with methods for submit, poll, fetch result, and cancel/timeout handling if supported.
- [ ] Add tests for success, pending timeout, rejected/failed policy result, auth failure, and malformed response.
- [ ] Wire the client into the planner-facing contract or CLI smoke command used by integration tests.
- [ ] Document required environment variables and local test command.

- [ ] A caller can submit a proposal and receive a stable proposal id through the client.
- [ ] Polling returns terminal approval/rejection/error states without throwing away the response body.

# Portal Flow Completion: Endpoint Contract, Validation, Templates, and Integration

## Why
PR #803 addressed issue #798, but verification identified remaining gaps and the verdict was **FAIL**. This follow-up focuses on completing the portal flow against the required endpoint contract, validation behavior, rendering split, shared integration paths, auth expectations, cleanup, tests, and documentation with a clearer task structure.

## Source
- Original PR: #803
- Parent issue: #798

## Scope
Refactor the browser portal flow to:
- Expose `GET /portal/draft/new`, `POST /portal/draft`, and `GET /portal/review/{draft_id}`
- Remove legacy `/portal/requests/*` route wiring
- Enforce required-field validation via `prompt_flow.py` before any draft persistence with HTTP 400 HTML responses listing missing fields
- Split rendering into distinct templates (`templates/draft_entry.html`, `templates/validation_feedback.html`, `templates/review_summary.html`)
- Build review state via `canonical.py` and `policy_api.py` without duplicating their logic and while preserving the `policy_api.py` contract
- Remove planner bearer-token authorization requirements from `POST /portal/draft`
- Clean up unused helpers and replace bare `assert` in `_portal_artifacts` with runtime exceptions
- Update tests and documentation (`docs/workflows.md`, `docs/plan.md`) accordingly

## Non-Goals
- No new portal features beyond the required endpoint contract, validation behavior, template split, and related refactors
- No changes to the existing `policy_api.py` external contract beyond internal integration
- No retention/aliasing of legacy `/portal/requests/*` routes

## Tasks

### Route Registration
- [ ] Register new portal routes for GET /portal/draft/new, POST /portal/draft, and GET /portal/review/{draft_id} in the app router module
- [ ] Remove all legacy /portal/requests/* route registrations from the app router and route registration modules
- [ ] Verify that no active route registration exists for /portal/requests/* endpoints after removal

### Validation Implementation
- [ ] Implement required-field validation in the `POST /portal/draft` handler by calling `prompt_flow.py` before any draft persistence call
- [ ] Add logic to return HTTP 400 when `prompt_flow.py` reports missing fields, rendering an HTML `<ul>` with one `<li>` per missing field
- [ ] Ensure no draft persistence method is called when validation fails

### Template Creation
- [ ] Create templates/draft_entry.html template file with appropriate structure for draft form entry
- [ ] Create templates/validation_feedback.html template file with structure for displaying validation errors in a ul/li format
- [ ] Create templates/review_summary.html template file with structure for displaying draft review information

### Handler Updates
- [ ] Update GET /portal/draft/new handler to render templates/draft_entry.html
- [ ] Update POST /portal/draft handler to render templates/validation_feedback.html when validation fails
- [ ] Update GET /portal/review/{draft_id} handler to render templates/review_summary.html

### Review Integration
- [ ] Update the `GET /portal/review/{draft_id}` handler to build review state by calling integration points in `canonical.py` and `policy_api.py` without inline canonicalization/policy evaluation logic
- [ ] Verify that the existing `policy_api.py` contract is preserved for existing callers and tests

### Authorization
- [ ] Remove planner bearer-token authorization middleware/decorators from the `POST /portal/draft` route
- [ ] Update auth-related tests to verify `POST /portal/draft` accepts requests without an `Authorization` header

### Code Cleanup
- [ ] Remove _portal_answers_from_form function if it has no remaining references in the codebase
- [ ] Replace all bare assert statements in _portal_artifacts with explicit runtime exceptions
- [ ] Add unit tests to verify that _portal_artifacts runtime exceptions fire under python -O optimization mode

### Test Updates
- [ ] Update existing portal route tests to use new route names /portal/draft/new, /portal/draft, and /portal/review/{draft_id}
- [ ] Remove all test references and assertions that rely on legacy /portal/requests/* route names
- [ ] Add automated test verifying that missing-field submission to POST /portal/draft returns HTTP 400 without redirect
- [ ] Add automated test verifying that missing-field response contains a ul element with li entries for each missing field
- [ ] Add automated test verifying that successful POST /portal/draft submission redirects to /portal/review/{draft_id}

### Documentation
- [ ] Update docs/workflows.md to document the three portal endpoints GET /portal/draft/new, POST /portal/draft, and GET /portal/review/{draft_id}
- [ ] Update docs/plan.md to document HTTP 400 behavior for missing required fields including the ul/li HTML structure

- [ ] Update docs/workflows.md to describe the existence of separate templates for entry, validation feedback, and review states
- [ ] Update docs/plan.md to describe the existence of separate templates for entry, validation feedback, and review states

## Acceptance Criteria

### Route Behavior
- [ ] A `GET` request to `/portal/draft/new` returns HTTP 200 and is not a redirect
- [ ] `GET /portal/draft/new` renders `templates/draft_entry.html`
- [ ] A `POST` request to `/portal/draft` with a valid form submission returns an HTTP redirect to `/portal/review/{draft_id}` where `{draft_id}` is the created draft identifier
- [ ] A `GET` request to `/portal/review/{draft_id}` for an existing draft returns HTTP 200
- [ ] `GET /portal/review/{draft_id}` renders `templates/review_summary.html`
- [ ] No active portal route registration exists for legacy `/portal/requests/*` endpoints

### Validation Behavior
- [ ] When required fields are missing, `POST /portal/draft` returns HTTP 400 and does not return a redirect status
- [ ] For a submission missing required fields, the `POST /portal/draft` response body contains exactly one `<li>` element for each missing field reported by `prompt_flow.py`, wrapped inside a `<ul>` element
- [ ] Invalid `POST /portal/draft` renders `templates/validation_feedback.html`
- [ ] When `prompt_flow.py` reports missing required fields, no draft persistence method is called during `POST /portal/draft` handling
- [ ] The `POST /portal/draft` handler invokes `prompt_flow.py` validation before any call to draft persistence for every submission path

### Template Files
- [ ] The codebase contains `templates/draft_entry.html`
- [ ] The codebase contains `templates/validation_feedback.html`
- [ ] The codebase contains `templates/review_summary.html`

### Integration
- [ ] The review route handler contains no inline canonicalization or policy evaluation logic and instead calls integration points in `canonical.py` and `policy_api.py` to build the review state
- [ ] Existing callers/tests for `policy_api.py` continue to use the same route/response contract after the portal review integration change

### Authorization
- [ ] A `POST /portal/draft` request without any `Authorization` header is processed by the route handler and is not rejected with 401 or 403
- [ ] The `POST /portal/draft` route is not decorated with, wrapped by, or registered behind planner bearer-token authorization middleware

### Code Cleanup
- [ ] No function or symbol named `_portal_answers_from_form` remains referenced anywhere in the application code
- [ ] The `_portal_artifacts` implementation contains no bare `assert` statements
- [ ] When an `_portal_artifacts` invariant/error condition is triggered, the code raises an explicit runtime exception in both normal and optimized Python execution modes

### Test Coverage
- [ ] Portal route tests cover `GET /portal/draft/new`, `POST /portal/draft`, and `GET /portal/review/{draft_id}` and do not rely on `/portal/requests/*` route names
- [ ] At least one automated test verifies missing-field submission to `POST /portal/draft` returns HTTP 400, does not redirect, and includes a `<ul>` with the expected missing-field entries
- [ ] At least one automated test verifies a successful `POST /portal/draft` submission redirects to `/portal/review/{draft_id}`

### Documentation
- [ ] `docs/workflows.md` documents the portal endpoints `GET /portal/draft/new`, `POST /portal/draft`, and `GET /portal/review/{draft_id}` exactly
- [ ] `docs/plan.md` documents that missing required fields on `POST /portal/draft` produce HTTP 400 and an HTML response containing a `<ul>` with one entry per missing field, and that no draft is saved in that case
- [ ] Both `docs/workflows.md` and `docs/plan.md` explicitly describe the existence of separate templates for entry, validation feedback, and review states

## Implementation Notes

### Route Registration
Use the app portal router module(s), main app route registration file, and route-related tests to complete the endpoint refactor. Ensure all browser portal routing uses the canonical paths `/portal/draft/new`, `/portal/draft`, and `/portal/review/{draft_id}`, and remove legacy `/portal/requests/*` registrations rather than aliasing them if that would keep old routes active.

### Validation Flow
In the portal `POST /portal/draft` handler, invoke `prompt_flow.py` validation before any create/save call in the draft persistence or service layer. For missing required fields, return HTTP 400 with an HTML response rendered from a dedicated validation template containing a single `<ul>` with one `<li>` per missing field. Do not persist invalid drafts.

### Templates
Create or update these templates:
- `templates/draft_entry.html`
- `templates/validation_feedback.html`
- `templates/review_summary.html`

### Review Integration
Route handlers should contain no inline canonicalization or policy evaluation logic and instead delegate to `canonical.py` and `policy_api.py` integration points. For review construction, call into `canonical.py` and `policy_api.py` integration points/adaptors instead of reproducing canonicalization or policy evaluation logic inline in the route body. Preserve the current `policy_api.py` contract for existing callers and tests.

### Authorization
Remove planner bearer-token authorization requirements specifically from the browser portal draft submission route so `POST /portal/draft` is usable without auth headers. Update auth-related tests accordingly.

### Code Cleanup
Remove `_portal_answers_from_form` if it is unused, and replace bare asserts in `_portal_artifacts` with explicit runtime exceptions that still fire under optimized execution (for example, under `python -O`). Add unit tests for those error paths.

### Testing
Update portal route tests, functional/integration tests for form submission, and any fixtures with hard-coded old route names. Prefer tests that assert rendered template identity or stable page markers, verify redirect locations, inspect route registration, and use mocks/spies to confirm validation ordering and no-save behavior on invalid submissions.

### Documentation
Update `docs/workflows.md` and `docs/plan.md` rather than limiting documentation changes to README content.

### Context from Previous Attempt
- Previous attempt implemented route paths under `/portal/requests/` instead of the required `/portal/draft` and `/portal/review` endpoints. Strictly conform to `/portal/draft/new`, `POST /portal/draft`, and `/portal/review/{draft_id}`.
- Previous attempt handled missing fields by always saving the draft and redirecting. Instead, validate immediately inside the POST handler, return HTTP 400 with detailed error HTML, and do not save any draft when required fields are missing.

## Deferred Tasks (Requires Human)
None

# Add Minimal Workflow Portal for Travel Request Submission

## Why

The repository has strong domain logic, planner-facing APIs, spreadsheet export, and policy evaluation, but it still does not provide the lightweight end-user workflow portal implied by the Stage 2 plan. That leaves the repo usable as a backend package, but not yet as a complete travel request product.

## Scope

Introduce a minimal workflow portal attached to the existing FastAPI runtime so employees can start a travel request, review policy readiness, and submit a request through a real UI instead of only through fixtures or direct API calls.

## Non-Goals

- Building a large SPA or separate frontend stack
- Implementing accounting reimbursement in the same issue
- Replacing the canonical spreadsheet/export pipeline

## Tasks

### Portal Routes
- [ ] Create GET route for displaying the draft creation form in `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py`
- [ ] Create POST route for handling draft submission in `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py`
- [ ] Create GET route for displaying the review screen in `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py`
- [ ] Mount all new portal routes on the existing FastAPI app instance

### HTML Templates
- [ ] Create HTML template for the draft entry form with all required input fields under `src/travel_plan_permission/templates/`
- [ ] Create HTML template for displaying validation feedback and missing field errors under `src/travel_plan_permission/templates/`
- [ ] Create HTML template for the request review and summary screen under `src/travel_plan_permission/templates/`

### Draft Handling Logic
- [ ] Implement draft data model to capture trip details, travel purpose, and cost context
- [ ] Integrate `src/travel_plan_permission/canonical.py` seams to validate and normalize draft input data
- [ ] Integrate `src/travel_plan_permission/prompt_flow.py` to identify missing required fields in draft submissions
- [ ] Add error handling and user-friendly error messages for validation failures

### Policy Integration
- [ ] Update the portal review route to display policy-readiness diagnostics by reusing `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py` instead of duplicating policy logic

### Tests
- [ ] Add test for successful draft creation POST request with valid inputs under `tests/python/`
- [ ] Add test for draft creation POST with missing required fields returns validation errors under `tests/python/`
- [ ] Add test for validation error rendering displays correct missing field messages under `tests/python/`
- [ ] Add test for review page rendering displays draft data and policy readiness status under `tests/python/`

### Documentation
- [ ] Update `docs/workflows.md` with steps to run the portal locally via the standard service workflow
- [ ] Update `docs/plan.md` with portal architecture and integration points

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The portal serves a draft creation form at `/portal/draft/new`, accepts POST submissions to `/portal/draft`, and displays a review screen at `/portal/review/{draft_id}` with data from `canonical.py` and `policy_api.py`
- [ ] When required inputs are missing, the portal returns HTTP 400 with an HTML response containing a list element for each missing field identified by `prompt_flow.py`, and the form is not submitted to the backend
- [ ] The portal's policy-readiness and canonical evaluation paths call into `src/travel_plan_permission/canonical.py`, `src/travel_plan_permission/prompt_flow.py`, and `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py` (no duplicated policy/canonical logic in route handlers)
- [ ] All tests under `tests/python/` pass, covering draft creation, validation feedback rendering, and review-state rendering

## Implementation Notes

### Relevant Files
- `src/travel_plan_permission/http_service.py` - Add portal routes
- `src/travel_plan_permission/prompt_flow.py` - Reuse for missing field identification
- `src/travel_plan_permission/canonical.py` - Reuse for data validation and normalization
- `src/travel_plan_permission/policy_api.py` - Reuse for policy-readiness diagnostics
- `src/travel_plan_permission/templates/` - Create new HTML templates
- `tests/python/test_http_service.py` - Extend with portal tests
- `tests/python/` - Add new portal route/UI tests

### Reference Documentation
- `docs/plan.md` - Stage 2 plan context
- `docs/workflows.md` - Service workflow documentation
- `docs/policy-api.md` - Policy evaluation integration

### Architecture Notes
The portal should be implemented as server-rendered routes using FastAPI's template support (Jinja2). All business logic should delegate to existing modules (`canonical.py`, `prompt_flow.py`, `policy_api.py`) to avoid duplication. The draft data model should align with the canonical trip schema to ensure consistency with the existing spreadsheet export pipeline.

## Deferred Tasks (Requires Human)

None - all tasks are implementable by a coding agent.

## Scope

Sequence the remaining repo-side work required to make
`Travel-Plan-Permission` testable as a live planner-facing service for
`trip-planner`, from HTTP runtime through auth/bootstrap, smoke validation, and
operator-facing documentation.

## Non-Goals

- Reworking `trip-planner` UI or persistence behavior
- Full production deployment hardening or enterprise tenancy
- Replacing the canonical planner-facing contracts already established in #744-#748
- Building admin-only policy management surfaces unrelated to planner testing

## Tasks

- [ ] #783 [Agent] [Service Runtime] Expose the planner-facing policy API through a runnable HTTP service
- [ ] #784 [Agent] [Security] Add live-test auth bootstrap and startup validation for planner endpoints
- [ ] #785 [Agent] [Integration] Add end-to-end planner HTTP smoke coverage for live testing
- [ ] #786 [Agent] [Docs] Publish a live-test runbook and repo-native entrypoints for planner integration

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All child issues needed for live planner-service testing are completed.
- [ ] A developer can start a planner-facing TPP service from this repo using documented commands only.
- [ ] `trip-planner` can target the repo through a real HTTP base URL and documented auth configuration.
- [ ] One blessed smoke path proves the planner handshake over HTTP instead of relying only on in-process contract builders.

## Implementation Notes

- Build on the completed planner API stabilization epic `#744` and child issues `#745`-`#748` rather than replacing their contract decisions.
- Child order matters: runtime service first, then auth/bootstrap, then smoke coverage, then operator docs that point to the final blessed path.

- Keep the runtime surface narrow and planner-facing; the goal is live-test readiness, not a broad new product surface.

```markdown
## Why
PR #301 addressed issue #297 but verification identified concerns (verdict: **CONCERNS**). This follow-up addresses the remaining gaps with improved task structure to ensure the LangGraph integration is properly validated and tested in the CI environment.

## Tasks
- [ ] Update the CI configuration to include a job that runs `pip install .[orchestration]` and executes the LangGraph-path test.
- [ ] Modify the LangGraph-path test module to remove or conditionally bypass the use of `pytest.importorskip` if running in CI.
- [ ] Add tests to `src/travel_plan_permission/orchestration/graph.py` to verify that when `prefer_langgraph` is True, the LangGraph compiled codepath is executed and the correct artifact is generated.
- [ ] Review and update the test suite configuration to ensure that new test modules are included in the test runs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The CI configuration includes a job that runs `pip install .[orchestration]` and executes the LangGraph-path test module without skipping any tests.
- [ ] The LangGraph-path test module does not use `pytest.importorskip` when running in the CI environment.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/orchestration_graph_test.py` verify that when `prefer_langgraph` is True, the LangGraph compiled codepath is executed and the correct artifact is generated.

## Implementation Notes
- Modify `tests/langgraph_path_test.py` to conditionally bypass `pytest.importorskip`.
- Add new tests in `tests/orchestration_graph_test.py` to cover the `prefer_langgraph` logic.
- Ensure `pytest.ini` and `setup.cfg` are updated to include new test modules.

<details>
<summary>Background (previous attempt context)</summary>

- **What failed:** Relying solely on `pytest.importorskip('langgraph')` in tests.
  - **Why it failed:** This approach leads to tests being skipped if the CI environment does not install the orchestration dependency, giving a false pass.
  - **What to try instead:** Explicitly install the dependency in the CI job and adjust test logic to affirm the execution of the LangGraph code path, preventing automatic skipping.

- **What failed:** Merging CI workflow changes without confirming that job execution properly installs the extra.
  - **Why it failed:** An in-progress workflow or misconfigured job can mask real integration issues with the orchestration extra installation.
  - **What to try instead:** Ensure that the CI configuration includes a separate, confirmed job that installs the orchestration extra and logs the output to verify the dependency’s availability before running tests.

</details>
```

## Why
Current TripState contains Path and a full TripPlan object. That’s fine for a demo, but it becomes annoying when you want checkpointing, persistence, or tooling that expects JSON-serializable state.

## Scope
Make orchestration state safe to serialize via model_dump(mode="json") and json.dumps(...).

Avoid non-JSON-native types in state (Path, raw Decimal/date not encoded, etc.).

## Non-Goals
Implementing a persistent checkpointer backend (SQLite/Postgres/etc.) unless it’s needed to validate serialization correctness.

Refactoring the entire policy layer.

## Tasks
- [ ] Replace Path fields in state with str (or structured artifact metadata objects that serialize cleanly).
- [ ] Decide how to represent plan data in state:
  - Option A: keep TripPlan but ensure dumps are JSON-safe, or
  - Option B: store plan_json dict + validate/construct TripPlan at node boundaries.
- [ ] Ensure canonical intake representation in state is also JSON-safe (dict or pydantic model dump).
- [ ] Add a test asserting json.dumps(state.model_dump(mode="json")) succeeds for a “realistic” run.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] TripState.model_dump(mode="json") produces JSON-serializable output (no TypeError on json.dumps(...)).
- [ ] No Path objects or other arbitrary types remain in state.
- [ ] CI passes.

## Implementation Notes
Relevant files:
- src/travel_plan_permission/orchestration/graph.py
- tests/python/ (new test file, likely test_orchestration_state_serialization.py)

body:
## Problem

The `agents-issue-intake.yml` workflow is experiencing **startup_failure** errors on all runs. Analysis shows this is caused by a YAML syntax error.

**Root Cause:** Line 109 has an improperly wrapped `if` condition where `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` appears on the same line as the condition's closing parenthesis, violating YAML syntax rules.

## Current Code (Lines 107-110)
```yaml
  check_labels:
    needs: route
    if: needs.route.outputs.should_run_bridge == 'true' && (github.event_name != 'issues' || contains(toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name), 'agent:') || contains(toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name), 'agents:'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
```

## Fixed Code
```yaml
  check_labels:
    needs: route
    if: |
      needs.route.outputs.should_run_bridge == 'true' &&
      (github.event_name != 'issues' ||
       contains(toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name), 'agent:') ||
       contains(toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name), 'agents:'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
```

## Solution

Apply the patch file attached below, or wait for the next template sync from stranske/Workflows which includes this fix (PR #602).

### Manual Fix
```bash
# Edit .github/workflows/agents-issue-intake.yml
# Replace lines 108-109 with the fixed code above
```

## Testing
- ✅ YAML syntax validation passes
- ✅ Workflow will start successfully after fix

## Related
- Template fix PR: stranske/Workflows#602
- Failing runs: https://github.com/stranske/Travel-Plan-Permission/actions/workflows/agents-issue-intake.yml

---
**Patch file:**
```diff
diff --git a/.github/workflows/agents-issue-intake.yml b/.github/workflows/agents-issue-intake.yml
index 3f341a4..3aace46 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/agents-issue-intake.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/agents-issue-intake.yml
@@ -106,7 +106,11 @@ jobs:
   # Gate for agent_bridge mode: only proceed if issue has agent:* or agents:* label
   check_labels:
     needs: route
-    if: needs.route.outputs.should_run_bridge == 'true' && (github.event_name != 'issues' || contains(toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name), 'agent:') || contains(toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name), 'agents:'))
+    if: |
+      needs.route.outputs.should_run_bridge == 'true' &&
+      (github.event_name != 'issues' ||
+       contains(toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name), 'agent:') ||
+       contains(toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name), 'agents:'))
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     outputs:
       should_run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.should_run }}
```
